dz.headline: Mauritania thanks Algeria for OIC Secretary General election support
dz.dek: Mauritania's Foreign Minister, Mohamed Salem Ould Marzouk, expressed gratitude to Algeria for its backing of Ismail Ould Cheikh Ahmed's election as the new Secretary General.
paragraphs: Mauritania acknowledged Algeria's support for its candidate, Ismail Ould Cheikh Ahmed, who was elected Secretary General of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC). This appreciation was conveyed by Mauritanian Foreign Minister Mohamed Salem Ould Marzouk during discussions with Algerian Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, National Community Abroad, and African Affairs, Ahmed Attaf, on Thursday, August twenty-seventh.

The meeting took place in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, on the sidelines of the twenty-third extraordinary session of the OIC Council of Foreign Ministers. Ould Marzouk highlighted Ould Cheikh Ahmed's competence and experience, stating these qualities would enable him to fulfill his duties effectively and enhance the organization's work and objectives.

In response, Attaf congratulated Mauritania on the election of its candidate and reaffirmed Algeria's readiness to collaborate and coordinate with the new Secretary General. This cooperation aims to serve the OIC's goals and principles, strengthening its role in advocating for the issues and interests of the Islamic world's peoples, according to the Algerian Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

dz.headline: US Embassy offers condolences to Algeria after deadly fires
dz.dek: The US Embassy in Algeria expressed sympathy for the victims of tragic fires that claimed 12 lives across several provinces, prompting a three-day national mourning period.
paragraphs: The US Embassy in Algeria extended its condolences on Thursday to the country following tragic fires that affected several provinces. The embassy conveyed its sincere sympathy and solace to the families of the victims and wished a swift and full recovery to all those injured.

The fires resulted in the deaths of 12 people, as confirmed by Interior Minister Said Sayoud on Wednesday evening from Bejaia. The President of the Republic, Abdelmadjid Tebboune, had earlier declared a three-day national mourning period in remembrance of those who perished.

The declaration of national mourning underscores the severity of the incident and the impact on the affected communities. The US Embassy's message highlights international acknowledgment of the tragedy and support for Algeria during this difficult time.

dz.headline: Algeria observes deep partial lunar eclipse on Friday
dz.dek: A very deep partial lunar eclipse will be visible from Algeria on Friday, August twenty-eighth, two thousand twenty-six, according to the Astronomy, Astrophysics and Geophysics.
paragraphs: The moon will enter the Earth's penumbra at two twenty-three AM local time in Algeria, followed by its entry into the Earth's shadow around three thirty-three AM. The eclipse will reach its maximum at five thirteen AM local time, when the moon will be very low in the sky.

The moon will set around six twenty-two AM, before the partial phase is expected to end around six fifty-one AM. This eclipse is considered a distinctive astronomical phenomenon for observation and photography, provided there is a western horizon completely free of obstructions.

The Astronomy, Astrophysics and Geophysics Research Center stated that the lunar eclipse can be safely observed with the naked eye without any risk to the eyes, and without the need for special glasses. The eclipse will not be total, with about ninety-six point three percent of the moon's disk falling within the Earth's shadow at the peak of the astronomical event.

dz.headline: Wildfires Close Roads in Skikda, Annaba, and El Tarf
dz.dek: Multiple roads, including sections of the East-West Highway, were closed on Thursday, August twenty-seventh, due to fires in Skikda, Annaba, and El Tarf provinces.
paragraphs: The National Gendarmerie's Traffic Information and Coordination Center announced road closures across several provinces due to ongoing fires. In Skikda, the East-West Highway was closed at the Ain Charshar interchange towards Annaba, diverting traffic to National Road 44. Another section of the East-West Highway at the Ghadir interchange, also towards Annaba, saw traffic rerouted to National Road 44A.

In Annaba province, the East-West Highway was closed at the Ain El Barda interchange towards Skikda and El Tarf, with traffic diverted to National Roads 21 and 84. Additionally, fires closed Provincial Road 107 between the municipalities of Triat and Chetaibi, National Road 84 between National Roads 44 and 21 in El Alma municipality, and Provincial Road 167 between Berrahal and Oued El Annab municipalities.

El Tarf province also experienced closures, with the East-West Highway shut down at the Dhraan interchange towards Annaba, diverting traffic to National Road 84. National Road 82, connecting the municipalities of El Tarf and Zitouna, was also closed, with traffic rerouted to Provincial Road 105 towards the municipalities of Asfour and Bouhadjar in El Tarf province, according to Echorouk Online.

dz.headline: Niger's Prime Minister Concludes Official Visit to Algeria
dz.dek: Ali Mahamane Lamine Zeine, Prime Minister of Niger, departed Algeria on Thursday evening following an official visit with a significant delegation.
paragraphs: Prime Minister Ali Mahamane Lamine Zeine of Niger concluded his official visit to Algeria on Thursday, August twenty-seventh, departing from Houari Boumediene International Airport. He was seen off by Algerian Prime Minister Seifi Gharib.

The Algerian delegation bidding farewell included several key ministers: Mohamed Arkab, Minister of State and Minister of Hydrocarbons; Abedkarim Bouzard, Minister of Finance; Mourad Adjal, Minister of Energy and Renewable Energies; Sid Ali Zerrougui, Minister of Post and Telecommunications; and Abedlkader Djellaoui, Minister of Public Works and Basic Infrastructure.

Also present were Karima Bekir Tafer, Secretary of State to the Minister of Mines and Mining Industries; Major General Mohamed Saleh Ben Bicha, Secretary General of the Ministry of National Defense; Boualem Chebihi, Director General for Africa at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs; and Ahmed Saadi, Algeria's Ambassador to Niger, underscoring the importance of the visit.

ao.headline: Angola hosts AU summit to adopt new conflict prevention strategy
ao.dek: Angola will host the African Union's first extraordinary summit on conflict prevention and resolution, aiming to shift from reactive to proactive crisis management.
paragraphs: The African Union will hold its first extraordinary summit on conflict prevention, management, and resolution in Luanda, Angola, on August twenty-ninth and thirtieth. This marks the first time since the AU's founding that heads of state will convene specifically on this issue, according to Miguel Bembe, Angola's ambassador to Ethiopia and spokesperson for the conference.

The summit's central objective is to transition from a reactive stance to a proactive, structural strategy for crisis prevention across the continent. Bembe stated that the meeting will conclude with the adoption of the Luanda Decision, complemented by Action Plans and an Implementation Matrix, which will clearly define objectives, targets, indicators, responsible parties, budgeting, and deadlines.

Bembe highlighted that these three documents represent an innovation, as previous extraordinary conferences typically adopted only a Political Declaration and a Decision. Angola proposed this new approach to ensure concrete results, with specific deadlines and monitoring mechanisms for implementation, addressing current challenges like weak coordination and underutilized operational structures.

bj.headline: Beninese TikToker Billy Acquitted of Internet Fraud Charges
bj.dek: Arsène Kplédo, known as Billy, was acquitted by the CRIET on Thursday, August twenty-seventh, 2026, due to insufficient evidence in a case of alleged internet fraud.
paragraphs: The Court of Repression of Economic Offenses and Terrorism (CRIET) acquitted Beninese content creator and TikToker Billy, whose real name is Arsène Kplédo, on Thursday, August twenty-seventh, 2026. He was cleared due to a lack of conclusive evidence regarding alleged internet fraud.

Kplédo had been awaiting the court's decision after being prosecuted for suspected internet fraud. The public prosecutor, during a previous hearing on July sixteenth, 2026, stated that the collected evidence did not establish the accused's guilt with certainty.
The CRIET followed the special prosecutor's analysis in its decision, ending the proceedings against Arsène Kplédo in this case. This ruling concludes the judicial episode for the content creator.

bj.headline: Benin military chief meets Pentagon to boost security cooperation
bj.dek: General Fructueux Gbaguidi, head of Benin's armed forces, met with US military leadership to deepen their partnership against regional security threats.
paragraphs: Benin's Chief of General Staff, General Fructueux Gbaguidi, met with General Christopher J. Mahoney, Vice Chairman of the US Joint Chiefs of Staff, at the Pentagon on Tuesday, August 25, 2026. Their discussions focused on security threats in West Africa, American assistance to Benin, and strengthening cooperation between the two armies.

The meeting reaffirmed the "strong and lasting" nature of the security partnership between Washington and Cotonou, according to an official US military report published the following day. Both officials addressed regional threats and the need for increased coordination with other West African partners.

This engagement follows recent joint activities, including a five-day exercise in late July where Beninese and American soldiers trained in detecting and neutralizing improvised explosive devices. The US considers Benin's stability important for regional security balance.

bj.headline: UBA Benin recruits legal assistant for compliance and litigation management

The role involves adapting the subsidiary's legal policies and procedures to group standards while ensuring adherence to all local legal requirements in Benin. This position will also manage relationships with the bank's legal partners, including lawyers and bailiffs.

The new assistant will be responsible for drafting legal documents, such as service and maintenance contracts, and monitoring litigation involving the bank and third parties or administrations. They will also provide specialized support on legal and intellectual property matters, and advise the General Management and other bank components on legal issues.

Key duties include managing legal reporting for the bank's affairs to General Management and regulatory bodies, identifying and evaluating legal and regulatory risks, and keeping management informed of local and international legal developments affecting the business. The assistant will also participate in negotiations and discussions, offering legal and strategic advice to the subsidiary.

bj.headline: Abdoulaye Bio Tchané visits artisan fair in Nikki
bj.dek: The President of the Economic and Social Council (CES), Abdoulaye Bio Tchané, toured the third regional artisan fair in Nikki, engaging with 75 exhibitors.
paragraphs: Abdoulaye Bio Tchané, President of the Economic and Social Council (CES), visited the third edition of the regional artisan fair in Nikki, Northern Benin, which runs from August twenty-first to August thirtieth, 2026. This visit followed his participation in the Gaani 2026 festivities and focused on understanding the local artisans' skills and working conditions.

The fair, organized by the Ministry of Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises and Employment Promotion, through the Artisan Development Fund, in collaboration with the Chamber of Trades and Crafts of Benin (CMA-Bénin), showcases textiles, sculptures, pottery, and jewelry. It aims to increase the visibility and commercialization of artisan products by leveraging the attendance of the Gaani cultural event.

Artisans expressed appreciation for the CES President's interest and advice, according to Biaou François Atchade, a Borgou departmental councilor for the CES and an artisan sector actor. They hope for continued support and the extension of the fair, aligning with the CES's renewed mission to engage with the population and address their realities.

bj.headline: Benin U20 women's team loses 3-2 to France in World Cup warm-up
bj.dek: The Beninese U20 women's national team, known as the Amazons, fell to France's U20 squad in a preparatory match for the 2026 U20 Women's World Cup.
paragraphs: Benin's U20 women's football team suffered a narrow 3-2 defeat against France at the National Football Centre in Clairefontaine. Romaine Gandonou scored both goals for Benin, who are preparing for the 2026 U20 Women's World Cup. The team, coached by Abdoulaye Ouzérou, initially took the lead in the eleventh minute.

France quickly responded, overturning the score to lead 2-1 by halftime. In the second half, Benin showed renewed determination, with Gandonou scoring her second goal in the seventy-fourth minute to equalize. However, France secured the winning goal ten minutes before the end of the match.

This match follows two significant victories for Benin against Sarcelles (7-2) and Fleury U19 (6-0). The team is scheduled to play one final preparatory match on Sunday against Paris FC U19 as they continue their training in France.

bw.headline: Chief Justice warns Law Society over Foot-and-Mouth Disease legal intervention
bw.dek: Chief Justice Gaolapelwe Ketlogetswe cautioned the Law Society of Botswana against interfering in a high-profile legal dispute concerning the Foot-and-Mouth Disease crisis.
paragraphs: Chief Justice Gaolapelwe Ketlogetswe issued a warning to the Law Society of Botswana (LSB) regarding its involvement in a significant legal case stemming from the Foot-and-Mouth Disease (FMD) outbreak. This caution followed Ketlogetswe's dismissal of an urgent application from the LSB, which sought to reverse his decision to allow South African Senior Counsel Reginald Willis to practice in Botswana on an ad hoc basis.

Willis had been granted permission to represent JS Beef (Pty) Ltd and Primefast (Pty) Ltd in urgent litigation. This litigation specifically addresses the government's management and the economic consequences of the FMD outbreak, indicating ongoing legal challenges related to the disease's impact.

The Chief Justice's stance underscores a judicial effort to manage the legal proceedings surrounding the FMD crisis, directly affecting companies involved in the beef industry and the broader economic implications of the outbreak.

bw.headline: Botswana's fertility rate drops below replacement level
bw.dek: Botswana's total fertility rate has fallen to 1.96 children per woman, indicating a potential future shortage of young people, according to Statistics Botswana.
paragraphs: Botswana faces a demographic shift as its total fertility rate has dropped below the replacement level of 2.1 children per woman. The 2024 Vital Statistics Report from Statistics Botswana indicates the rate now stands at 1.96 children per woman.

This decline suggests a future challenge for the country, which has historically focused on job creation for its youth. The slow, family-by-family change could lead to a different problem: a scarcity of young people in the population.

The long-term implications of this trend could affect the labor force and economic growth, shifting the national concern from youth unemployment to a potential shortage of young workers and consumers in the coming decades.

bw.headline: Government seeks P3.1 billion in August debt auction
bw.dek: The government plans to raise P3.1 billion from the domestic market on 28 August to finance its budget deficit, continuing its reliance on monthly debt auctions.
paragraphs: The government will conduct a debt auction on 28 August, aiming to raise P3.1 billion from the domestic market. This action continues the government's heavy reliance on monthly debt auctions to finance its budget deficit, according to the Sunday Standard.

The Bank of Botswana will manage the auction on behalf of the Ministry of Finance. The offering is part of the existing P55 billion domestic note programme and includes P1.5 billion in three-month Treasury bills maturing on 2 December 2026, and P1 billion in six-month bills maturing on 3 March 2027.

Additionally, the auction will include P600 million in reopened longer-term government bonds. This move highlights the government's ongoing strategy to secure funds from within the country to cover its financial obligations.

bw.headline: Foods Botswana faces scrutiny after rodent discovery in children's food
bw.dek: A food safety alert has been issued after dead rodents were reportedly found inside packaged Tsabana products, a government-supplied food for children.
paragraphs: Dozens of children are feared to have been exposed to a food safety risk following reports of dead rodents discovered within packaged Tsabana products. Tsabana is a government-supplied food product manufactured by Foods Botswana (Pty) Ltd, a subsidiary of Sefalana Holding Company Limited.

The discovery has prompted an urgent food safety alert and raised significant questions regarding the food safety controls at the Serowe-based manufacturer. The incident highlights potential vulnerabilities in the production and packaging processes of essential food items.

This event has drawn attention to the critical need for stringent quality assurance in food manufacturing, especially for products intended for vulnerable populations like children. The full extent of the exposure and its implications are under investigation.

bw.headline: Botswana's citizenship-for-investment program stalls, leaving applicants in limbo
bw.dek: The Impact Citizenship Program, designed to offer fast-track citizenship for financial contributions, has failed to launch on schedule and is not accepting applications.
paragraphs: Botswana's attempt to enter the global citizenship-by-investment market has stalled, with the much-promoted Impact Citizenship Program failing to open as scheduled. This delay has left prospective investors in an uncertain state, as the program, marketed as a gateway to citizenship in exchange for a financial contribution, remains non-operational.

According to DirectCitizenship.com, the government is still working to finalize the necessary legal, institutional, and administrative frameworks required to launch the scheme. What was advertised as a rapid entry into Botswana citizenship has instead become a prolonged delay, raising doubts about the program's readiness for international investors.

The program's inability to accept applications means that individuals who planned to invest in exchange for citizenship are currently unable to proceed. This situation contrasts sharply with the initial marketing of a fast-track process, creating uncertainty for those interested in the scheme.

bf.headline: Belgium reaffirms unconditional cooperation with Burkina Faso
bf.dek: Belgian Vice-Prime Minister Maxime Prévot stated his country's commitment to continue its cooperation with Burkina Faso without conditions after meeting with Burkinabè Foreign.
paragraphs: Belgium's Vice-Prime Minister, Maxime Prévot, reaffirmed his country's commitment to continue cooperation with Burkina Faso unconditionally during a 72-hour visit to Ouagadougou. This declaration followed discussions with Burkinabè Foreign Minister Karamoko Jean Marie Traoré, where Prévot emphasized the goal to "continue cooperation, not condition it."

The Belgian official explained that his visit aimed to gather firsthand information from Burkinabè authorities, comparing it with reports from Brussels. Minister Traoré welcomed this approach, highlighting the need for direct dialogue to understand African realities and presenting the context of the security crisis in Burkina Faso and the government's efforts to address it.

Discussions also covered the dynamics of the Sahel States Confederation (AES) and future cooperation between Burkina Faso and the European Union. Prévot stated Belgium's intent to invest "in Burkina Faso, with Burkina Faso, but not in place of Burkina Faso," underscoring a bilateral relationship spanning over 50 years, primarily through the Belgian development agency Enabel, across various sectors including economic development, agriculture, health, and education.

bf.headline: BMCRF sells 100 tonnes of seized rice at social prices starting September 1, 2026
bf.dek: The Mobile Brigade for Economic Control and Fraud Repression (BMCRF) announced it will sell 100 tonnes of rice, confiscated due to clandestine storage, at social prices.
paragraphs: The BMCRF will begin selling 100 tonnes of seized rice at social prices on September 1, 2026, according to a communiqué published on August 27, 2026. This initiative follows the confiscation of the rice due to clandestine storage. Interested individuals can subscribe in advance at the BMCRF offices, located opposite the former Primature, from 9 hours to 15 hours daily until stocks are depleted.

The proceeds from this sale will be fully transferred to the Patriotic Support Fund (FSP). The BMCRF also stated that controls are ongoing, and any offenders will face sanctions in accordance with current regulations. The public is encouraged to report suspicious cases using the green numbers 80 00 11 84/85/86.

This action comes as regional authorities, such as the Tannounyan regional directorate of industry, commerce, and crafts, are conducting price and quality controls in Banfora. On August 24, 2026, officials visited over a dozen businesses to ensure compliance with state-fixed prices and hygiene standards, warning that non-compliant merchants face fines and community service.

bf.headline: Burkina Faso trains 2,246 youth in national identity and sovereignty
bf.dek: The second edition of the Compulsory Patriotic Immersion program concluded on Thursday, August twenty-seventh, 2026, after a month of civic and patriotic training for new high.
paragraphs: Two thousand two hundred forty-six high school graduates from the Goulmou, Sirba, and Tapoa regions completed their compulsory patriotic immersion in Fada N’Gourma. The program, which ran from July twenty-seventh to August twenty-sixth, 2026, focused on national identity, citizenship, and sovereignty, with one thousand seven hundred seventy-three participants from the Goulmou region alone.

The closing ceremony was presided over by the Governor of the Goulmou region, Ram Joseph Kafando, alongside administrative, military, paramilitary, religious, and customary authorities. Participants demonstrated knowledge and values acquired during the month-long training, which included discipline, love of country, Burkinabè history, and military and civic instruction.

Military instructor Lieutenant Boureima Ouédraogo stated the training covered discipline, weapons handling, and social cohesion, as well as civics, road safety, health, and hygiene. Governor Kafando urged the graduates to become “ambassadors of peace and love of country” and models of conduct in their future endeavors.

bf.headline: Burkinabe Handball Team Seeks Blessings from Mogho-Naba for Upcoming Tournament
bf.dek: The Burkina Faso women's national handball team, the Étalons dames, visited Mogho-Naba Baongho to receive his blessings before hosting the IHF Nation Trophy Zone 3 tournament.
paragraphs: The Étalons dames, Burkina Faso's national women's handball team, met with His Majesty Mogho-Naba Baongho at his royal palace in Ouagadougou on August twenty-sixth. The team sought his blessings ahead of the IHF Nation Trophy Seniors Zone 3 tournament, which Burkina Faso will host from September two to six. This visit is a customary practice for regional or international competitions, according to Boubakar Sanfo, president of the Burkinabe Handball Federation (FBH).

The upcoming tournament will feature eight nations from Zone 3, including Ghana, Côte d'Ivoire, Benin, Niger, Nigeria, Togo, Liberia, and Burkina Faso. The Burkinabe players are currently in residential training, aiming to win the trophy and qualify for the Africa Cup of Nations (CAN) in handball. Sanfo stated that winning this first edition of the tournament is their objective.

During the audience, Mogho-Naba Baongho offered advice to the players and staff, urging them to play without worry and maintain team cohesion. He emphasized the importance of defending the national colors with honor. Captain and goalkeeper Orokia Kazony expressed gratitude for the blessings and advice, stating the team is prepared and confident to compete.

bf.headline: SONABEL opens Bagré dam gates early, warns of flood risks
bf.dek: Burkina Faso's national electricity company, SONABEL, will open the Bagré hydroelectric dam's floodgates on Friday, August twenty-eighth, 2026, due to critical water levels.
paragraphs: SONABEL announced the early opening of the Bagré hydroelectric dam's floodgates, starting at nine hours on Friday, August twenty-eighth, 2026. This measure is necessary because recent heavy rainfall has caused the dam's water level to reach a critical threshold, requiring a faster evacuation of surplus water.

The company is urging communities living downstream from the dam to remain vigilant and take all necessary precautions. This warning comes as there is a risk of flooding resulting from the gate opening.

The decision to open the gates is a direct response to the elevated water levels in the reservoir. SONABEL's communication emphasizes the need for preparedness among the affected riverside populations.

bi.headline: Gitega residents discover two bodies, raising concerns about public violence
bi.dek: Two new bodies were found in Gitega province on Monday, August twenty-fourth, including one man allegedly beaten to death by residents for stealing rabbits.
paragraphs: The bodies were discovered in two localities within the central Burundi province. One victim, Népomucène Ntakarutimana, was found in the Kiruhura valley on Kiremera hill, reportedly beaten to death by angry residents after being caught attempting to steal rabbits from Anitha Nshimirimana, according to Kiremera hill chief Jean Claude Mfukamensabe. Jacqueline Ndayishimiye, Anitha Nshimirimana, and Arsène Ciza have been arrested in connection with this incident and are being held for investigation.

On the same day, a male infant's body was discovered in the Karonga valley, which separates the Yoba and Rukoba neighborhoods. The Gitega police confirmed this discovery, but the circumstances of the baby's death and the identities of those responsible remain unknown. The infant was buried on site as investigations continue to determine the exact cause of death and identify any responsible parties.

These discoveries follow two other deaths in Bugendana commune on Tuesday, August twenty-fifth, under distinct circumstances. The head of the Bugendana police post has been arrested as part of the investigation into these events. These incidents have renewed concerns about violence, security force interventions, and the increase in vigilantism and acts of popular justice in the province.

bi.headline: Burundian travelers face increased scrutiny and alleged extortion at Rwandan border
bi.dek: Burundian and Congolese travelers heading to Rwanda report intensified controls, repeated interrogations, and intimidation at border crossings, with some transporters allegedly.
paragraphs: Travelers from Burundi and Congo en route to Rwanda are experiencing heightened scrutiny and intimidation at border points, according to multiple testimonies collected by SOS Médias Burundi. Agents from the National Intelligence Service (SNR), supported by Imbonerakure youth league members, are reportedly conducting frequent checks and questioning individuals about their travel intentions to Rwanda.

Collective taxi drivers operating between Bujumbura and Kigali claim they are particularly targeted, facing accusations of transporting young people to the RED-Tabara armed group. Some drivers have been threatened, leading some transporters to change vehicles or suspend their services to avoid suspicion and harassment.

Transporters also allege they are being forced to pay significant sums of money to continue their activities. One driver in Muyinga stated that some transporters have paid up to one million Burundian francs to the police station in Muyinga to maintain their routes to Rwanda, indicating a potential racket affecting cross-border commerce.

bi.headline: Fire damages Kinindo market in Bujumbura, destroying goods and livelihoods
bi.dek: A fire on Tuesday ravaged a section of Kinindo market in southern Bujumbura, causing significant losses for several traders just days after another market fire in the city center.
paragraphs: A fire broke out around 10 o'clock in the Kinindo market, primarily affecting the mattress sales section. Firefighters, the Red Cross, and disaster management services responded quickly, bringing the flames under control within about an hour. However, a portion of the merchandise was destroyed, leaving many traders in shock over the loss of their goods and means of subsistence.

The incident follows a severe fire last Friday morning that devastated the Ndayizamba and Le Parisien commercial galleries in downtown Bujumbura. Finance Minister Alain Ndikumana visited the Kinindo site, stating that the cause of the fire is unknown and an investigation has begun. He assured that the government would monitor the situation and explore support measures for affected traders.

Antoine Muzaneza, president of the Association of Traders of Burundi (ACOBU), has called for concrete measures to enhance market security, including the creation of security committees and the implementation of controlled opening and closing hours. Traders are also requesting surveillance cameras to prevent future incidents and assist in identifying those involved in potential criminal acts, as attempts at theft occurred during the recent fire.

bi.headline: Burundi court imposes movement restrictions on provisional release
bi.dek: Individuals granted provisional release in Burundi must adhere to specific conditions, including restrictions on movement and contact, according to Iwacu.
paragraphs: Provisional release in Burundi now comes with strict conditions for the accused, including prohibitions on obstructing investigations or causing scandal through their conduct. They are also barred from visiting specific locations such as airports, ports, and train stations, or from being present there at designated times.

The accused must regularly report to the investigating magistrate or another official determined by the magistrate. They are also required to appear before the magistrate or judge whenever summoned and are forbidden from contacting victims or other specified individuals.

An order detailing these conditions is provided to the accused, who must sign it after notification. This notification of the provisional release order must occur within twenty-four hours, as reported by Iwacu.

cm.headline: MRC faces administrative challenge ahead of 2027 elections
cm.dek: The Minister of Territorial Administration has questioned recent actions by the Movement for the Rebirth of Cameroon (MRC), including the return of Maurice Kamto as party leader.
paragraphs: The Movement for the Rebirth of Cameroon (MRC) is navigating a critical period as the Minister of Territorial Administration has challenged its recent decisions. This administrative scrutiny, reported on August twenty-seventh, two thousand twenty-six, comes as the party prepares for legislative and municipal elections scheduled for two thousand twenty-seven.

The party, which boycotted elections for about five years, aims to re-engage in national and local power struggles. However, the decision to return Maurice Kamto to the party's leadership, following an internal crisis and purges of dissenting members, is now under official review. This situation creates uncertainty about the party's stability and its ability to field candidates.

The MRC also faces difficulties in presenting a presidential candidate for two thousand twenty-five due to a lack of elected officials and the challenge of gathering three hundred signatures from elected officials, first-degree traditional chiefs, or members of consular chambers. The party claims these administrative actions are attempts to destabilize it ahead of upcoming elections, according to Actu Cameroun.

cm.headline: Cameroon Revives Phone-Blocking Plan to Recover CFA25 Billion in Annual Customs Revenue
cm.dek: Cameroon will begin blocking undeclared mobile devices from local telecom networks on September 1, aiming to boost annual customs revenue by CFA25 billion.
paragraphs: Cameroon is set to implement a plan to block undeclared mobile phones, tablets, and other connected devices from its telecom networks starting September 1. This measure, announced by Finance Minister Louis Paul Motazé on August 20, comes three months after an initial enforcement deadline was missed.

The government expects this customs overhaul to generate CFA25 billion in annual revenue from mobile device imports. The restrictions will apply to devices that entered Cameroon without customs clearance after April 1, 2026, under a collection system established in the 2023 Finance Law and formally introduced in March 2026.

The blocking will affect undeclared devices connecting to a local telecom network for the first time, as well as phones activated after April 1 whose owners received warnings but did not comply. Devices activated in batches using the same SIM card after April 1 and no longer in continuous use are also included in the new policy.

cm.headline: UN Coordinator advocates pastoral mobility for climate adaptation in Cameroon
cm.dek: Issa Sanogo, the UN Resident Coordinator in Cameroon, urged for the preservation and facilitation of pastoral mobility as a critical climate adaptation strategy during the COP17.
paragraphs: During the COP17's Land and Peoples Day on August twenty-sixth, Issa Sanogo, the UN Resident Coordinator in Cameroon, highlighted pastoral mobility as a crucial climate adaptation strategy. He emphasized that this mobility should be facilitated, not restricted, to address desertification and strengthen community resilience.

Sanogo, speaking at a high-level roundtable on “Pastoralism for Resilience and Peace” organized by the IOM, called for a shift in perspective on pastoral mobility. He described pastoralism as a comprehensive socio-cultural and ecological system that secures sustainable livelihoods.

Drawing on Cameroon's experience with land pressure leading to tensions, Sanogo identified four key actions: securing access to pastoral lands and transhumance corridors, strengthening policy frameworks, improving data collection and early warning systems, and consolidating cross-border cooperation. These measures are deemed essential to prevent resource-related conflicts.

cm.headline: Cameroon boosts security for 2026 school and university re-entry
cm.dek: The Cameroonian government is increasing security measures nationwide ahead of the September 7, 2026 school re-entry and October university re-entry.
paragraphs: A special evaluation meeting on August 26, 2026, chaired by Minister Delegate to the Presidency in charge of Defense, Joseph Beti Assomo, addressed security concerns across the country. The meeting, held under high instructions from President Paul Biya, included key security and defense officials, such as the Minister of Territorial Administration and the Secretary of State for the National Gendarmerie.

While the overall security situation is deemed under control, specific areas of concern were highlighted. These include terrorist incursions in the Far North, persistent "dead city" orders in parts of the Northwest and Southwest, hostage-taking for ransom in the Septentrion region, and the security of borders, mining activities, and the maritime facade.

Authorities also discussed urban crime, specifically infanticides and femicides. In response to these challenges, the Minister of Defense ordered intensified security operations and improved coordination with administrative authorities to ensure a secure environment for students, teachers, and educational staff nationwide.

cf.headline: Central African Republic launches first National Tree and Forest Week
cf.dek: President Faustin Archange Touadera inaugurated the initiative in Bangui, aiming to promote afforestation and reforestation as a solution to climate change.
paragraphs: The Central African Republic launched its first National Tree and Forest Week (SNAF) on Monday, August 24, 2026, under the patronage of President Faustin Archange Touadera. The event, presided over by Prime Minister Félix Moloua, began with a tree planting ceremony on Bas-Oubangui hill in Bangui's seventh district, symbolizing a commitment to environmental health for residents and the planet.

This initiative, themed "Trees and forests for large-scale afforestation and reforestation: a solution for sustainable development," is part of a national strategy to combat climate change. Government officials emphasized that the SNAF aims to address deforestation and ecological fragility, which increase vulnerabilities in the country, by promoting collective mobilization.

The SNAF is intended to be an annual event, with activities planned throughout the week, including awareness campaigns, educational workshops, and community reforestation efforts. The government states its goal is to make every citizen an active participant in the fight against climate change, positioning environmental protection at the core of public policy for a greener future.

cf.headline: Bangui's Fondö residents decry months-long power outage
cf.dek: Residents in Bangui's Fondö district report being without electricity for several months, disrupting daily life and increasing insecurity concerns.
paragraphs: The Fondö district in Bangui's 3rd arrondissement has been without electricity for several months, according to residents. They attribute the ongoing power cut to Énergie centrafricaine (ENERCA), the national power utility, and state that the lack of power is severely impacting their daily routines and activities.

The prolonged outage has also heightened residents' fears regarding insecurity in the area. They are calling on ENERCA to restore electricity services promptly to alleviate the disruptions and address the safety concerns that have emerged due to the darkness.

This situation highlights a significant challenge for the community, as the absence of a reliable power supply affects both personal well-being and local commerce. The residents' appeal underscores the urgent need for intervention from the power company.

cf.headline: Central African Republic health sector faces persistent challenges
cf.dek: More than 100 days after the new government took office, citizens report ongoing issues with medicine shortages, insufficient medical staff, and high consultation costs.
paragraphs: The Central African Republic's health sector continues to struggle with significant difficulties, despite government efforts to rehabilitate some hospitals and announce new projects. Citizens across the country, including in Bangui and provincial cities, report that conditions for patient care have not substantially improved.

Patients frequently encounter medicine stockouts and a shortage of healthcare personnel in various health facilities. Simon-Pierre in Bangui acknowledged government efforts but stated that improvements remain insufficient, noting that the situation at the community hospital is largely unchanged since Médecins sans frontières departed.

Civil society organizations, such as "I Gué," led by Quentin Ngbouando, assess the outcomes as falling short of expectations. They highlight the high cost of care, maternal and neonatal deaths, inadequate medical equipment, and staff shortages as serious concerns, attributing these issues to the state's limited action in the sector.

cf.headline: CZ Empire trains Bangui residents in gift and money bouquet creation
cf.dek: CZ Empire is conducting a three-day workshop in Bangui to teach practical skills in crafting surprise gifts and money bouquets, aiming to foster income-generating activities.
paragraphs: CZ Empire, led by CEO Carole Zokoua, launched a three-day training workshop on Monday, August 24, at the Federation of Associations of Women Entrepreneurs of Central Africa (FAFECA) headquarters in Bangui. The initiative focuses on teaching participants how to make surprise gifts and money bouquets, with the goal of transforming creativity into entrepreneurial opportunities.

Over twenty people registered for the training, and more than fifteen attended the first day despite heavy rains in Bangui. The workshop is open to everyone, but young people and women, especially young girls, represent the majority of participants. Carole Zokoua, who received similar training abroad, aims to share her knowledge to help others start their own businesses.

Participants will learn the various steps involved in creating these items, with the objective of enabling them to produce their own creations by the end of the training. Certificates of participation will be awarded, providing attendees with a skill that can become a source of income, according to Zokoua.

km.headline: Reunion court orders Comorian soldier's expulsion after asylum denial
km.dek: A Comorian soldier, one of seven who deserted during military exercises in March, faces expulsion from La Réunion after his asylum request was rejected, maintaining his return.
paragraphs: A Comorian soldier will be expelled to the Comoros after a La Réunion administrative court upheld a judgment to return him, nearly four months after he deserted during the Papangue 2026 inter-army exercise. The soldier, born in 1997, arrived on the island on March twenty-second with a Comorian delegation for maneuvers and disappeared on March twenty-fourth. Seven soldiers deserted in total, with two found by the end of March, one of whom was already expelled to Moroni.

The soldier was apprehended on July twenty-second during an identity check and requested asylum on July twenty-fourth. His request was denied by the Ofpra on August sixth, followed by a prefectural order for his removal a week later. Before the judges, he claimed fear of an "extrajudicial execution" and stated he fled "exactions" by the army against the population, alleging he had information about a former colleague's assassination and another's disappearance.

The magistrates found his claims insufficiently documented to prove a personal and present danger, noting no appeal had been filed with the National Court of Asylum by the judgment date. The expulsion order remains in effect, and if returned, the soldier faces potential arrest upon arrival in the Comoros, where authorities have previously mentioned severe sanctions, including imprisonment and dismissal, for deserters.

km.headline: Mvola users credit Sonelec meters without payment, causing 200 million franc loss
km.dek: A malfunction between Mvola mobile payments and Sonelec prepaid electricity meters in Mohéli allowed multiple subscribers to credit their accounts without corresponding.
paragraphs: A payment system malfunction involving Mvola mobile payments and Sonelec prepaid electricity meters was observed in Mohéli on Tuesday, August eighteen. Several subscribers reportedly managed to credit their electricity meters without the corresponding amounts being debited from their Mvola accounts, according to Comores Infos.

The incident occurred hours after the restoration of Yas's money transfer service, which had been interrupted for maintenance. A source close to the matter estimates the potential financial damage at over 200 million Comorian francs. This source claims some users made multiple transactions, with one meter reportedly credited with more than nine million francs of electricity.

Neither Sonelec nor Yas had issued official statements regarding the incident as of the report's writing. The companies have not confirmed the figures or addressed how many meters are affected, whether the credits will be canceled, or if a technical investigation has been launched, leaving questions for subscribers and stakeholders.

cg.headline: Congo Senate approves four oil contract amendments
cg.dek: Senators in Brazzaville adopted four draft laws to adjust technical mechanisms related to "high price" clauses in oil production sharing contracts.
paragraphs: The Congolese Senate, led by President Pierre Ngolo, approved four draft laws on Wednesday, August twenty-sixth, 2026, during its third extraordinary session in Brazzaville. These laws concern amendments to oil production sharing contracts for the Nanga II bis, Nanga IV, Nanga V, and Marine XXIX-A permits.

The first two amendments, for Nanga II bis and Nanga IV, were signed on November twenty-third, 2023, between the Republic of Congo, the National Oil Company of Congo (SNPC), and China's Dingheng Mining Co. Ltd. The third amendment covers the Nanga V permit, and the fourth is for Marine XXIX-A, under a contract signed on April twenty-fifth, 2025, with Oriental Energy SAU.

These changes aim to adapt contractual provisions to current sector realities and encourage continued investment. The objective is to provide more visibility to operators and create favorable conditions for ongoing oil exploration, exploitation, and production activities, addressing economic, financial, industrial, budgetary, and social implications.

eg.headline: Health Ministry confirms no Salmonella outbreak in Egypt
eg.dek: Dr. Khaled Abdel Ghaffar, Minister of Health, stated that Egypt has not recorded any unusual Salmonella outbreaks despite international incidents.
paragraphs: The Egyptian Ministry of Health confirmed today that there is no Salmonella outbreak in the country, according to Minister of Health Dr. Khaled Abdel Ghaffar. The ministry is actively monitoring local and international health conditions through event-based epidemiological surveillance systems, specifically targeting foodborne illnesses like Salmonella.

Dr. Amr Kandil, Deputy Minister of Health, further noted that the Preventive Medicine and Public Health sector tracks daily changes in infection patterns and assesses reports based on established scientific standards. He confirmed that no unusual Salmonella outbreaks connected to recent international events have been recorded nationally.

This confirmation comes as the ministry reviews international incidents, including over 306 cases of Salmonella Enteritidis in Belgium and 207 confirmed cases in the United Kingdom, which led to product recalls. The ministry advises the public to follow essential food safety practices, such as thorough hand washing, separating raw and cooked foods, and purchasing items from trusted sources.

eg.headline: Egypt targets doubling oil and condensate output, advances $4bn refinery projects
eg.dek: Egypt aims to double its crude oil and condensate production through a five-year energy strategy while implementing six refinery projects with investments exceeding $4bn.
paragraphs: Egypt's presidency announced a new five-year energy strategy to double the country's crude oil and condensate output. President Abdel Fattah Al-Sisi reviewed the plans with Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly and Petroleum and Mineral Resources Minister Karim Badawi in New Alamein. The strategy includes seismic surveys, advanced technologies, and new contractual frameworks to develop discoveries and strengthen Egypt's position as a regional hub for petroleum product trading, gas liquefaction, and exports.

The government is also advancing six refinery projects with investments over $4bn to modernize existing facilities and increase domestic production of higher-value petroleum products. This initiative aims to reduce the country’s fuel import bill. Badawi also outlined plans for new wells expected to come online by December 2026 and development drilling in the Mediterranean.

Egypt seeks to attract further investment from international energy companies, having cleared overdue payments to foreign partners and maintaining regular payments on current obligations. Al-Sisi directed the government to provide more incentives for international partners to expand exploration and field development, and to increase the mining sector's contribution to the national economy.

eg.headline: Egypt urges global drought protocol ahead of COP18 presidency
eg.dek: Egypt's Water Resources and Irrigation Minister Hani Sewilam called for a legally binding international drought protocol at UNCCD COP17 in Mongolia.
paragraphs: Egypt has advocated for a legally binding international protocol on drought, stating that land degradation, desertification, and drought are direct threats to water and food security. Minister Hani Sewilam made this call during the ministerial segment of the 17th Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD COP17) in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia.

Sewilam emphasized that drought poses a serious threat to countries with acute water scarcity, such as Egypt, where available water resources are below the absolute water scarcity threshold and over 95% of the country is desert. He urged a shift from crisis response to prevention and preparedness, including stronger early-warning systems and integrated water and land resource management.

The minister also called for increased financing, clearer institutional mechanisms, and innovative financial instruments to support countries and communities most affected by drought and land degradation, particularly developing and African nations. He stressed the importance of restoring degraded land to strengthen food security, protect biodiversity, and preserve livelihoods.

eg.headline: British University in Egypt hosts All-Africa University Games torch relay
eg.dek: The British University in Egypt (BUE) in El Shorouk City hosted the torch relay for the 12th All-Africa University Games, “Cairo 2026,” on Wednesday.
paragraphs: The torch relay ceremony at BUE featured Olympic champion and university graduate Feryal Abdelaziz carrying the flame. This event is part of a national journey for the “Cairo 2026” torch, which started in the New Administrative Capital and is visiting major universities across Egypt, including The American University in Cairo and Cairo University.

The Games, held from 8 to 16 September 2026, mark the first time Egypt has hosted the continent’s largest multi-sport university competition. Approximately 2,000 student-athletes from 59 universities across 16 African countries will compete in 18 sports, with para-athletes included for the first time.

The ceremony was led by President and Vice-Chancellor Professor Mohamed Loutfi MBE, and attended by Professor Ashraf Sobhy, President of the Federation of Africa University Sports. The relay aligns with directives from Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi to showcase Egypt's standing in university sport.

paragraphs: The Egyptian Ministry of Youth and Sports has initiated legal action against wrestler Mohamed Mustafa Ali El-Shami following his defection during a transit layover in Rome. This referral to the Public Prosecution comes after El-Shami slipped away from his delegation while traveling from Taranto to Cairo. The delegation leader's attempt to retrieve him failed, leading the team coach to remain in Rome while the rest of the team returned home.

A separate case involving wrestler Ziad Haggag, who defected during the World Junior Wrestling Championships in Slovakia, has also been forwarded to prosecutorial authorities. The Ministry had previously instructed the Egyptian Wrestling Federation to investigate Haggag's disappearance and take appropriate legal measures. These actions follow preliminary investigations that indicated negligence and inadequate supervision of delegation members.

In response, the Egyptian Olympic Committee suspended Ibrahim Adel Ibrahim Mustafa Al-Attar, head of the wrestling delegation, and referred him to the Ethics Committee. Ministry officials emphasized that these incidents should not overshadow Egypt's strong performance at the Mediterranean Games, where the national wrestling team secured seven medals, including gold medals for Samar Hamza and Mohamed Hassan.

gq.headline: Equatorial Guinea Businesses Lose Value Due to Poor Public Perception
gq.dek: Many companies in Equatorial Guinea, despite years of operation and significant contributions, remain largely unknown outside their immediate circles, hindering their market.
paragraphs: Businesses in Equatorial Guinea are failing to translate their internal value into public recognition, according to a report from Ahora EG. The publication highlights that even companies with two decades of history and substantial contributions to economic activities often struggle with a weak or non-existent public presence.

This issue is not exclusive to large markets; it affects local businesses that are well-known by clients, suppliers, and employees but not by the broader market. The report suggests that while these companies may be extraordinary in their operations, their inability to effectively communicate their value prevents them from building a strong market position.

The problem is not a lack of activity or value creation, but rather a failure to make existing achievements visible. Effective business communication, the report notes, should consistently answer who a company is, what it does well, why it matters, and why it should be remembered, rather than just demonstrating activity.

gq.headline: Equatorial Guinea Government Removes Provincial Court President Over Abuse Case
gq.dek: The government dismissed Lucas Ela Meñe Bilingun from his recent appointment as president of the Provincial Courts of Bioko Norte, Bioko Sur, and Annobón due to a prior sexual.
paragraphs: The decision was made during a meeting at the People's Palace in Malabo, chaired by Vice President Teodoro Nguema Obiang. The government reviewed Bilingun's file, which revealed he had previously been prosecuted for sexually abusing a thirteen-year-old minor. Despite this record, he had been reinstated to positions of responsibility within the Justice Administration.

This action is part of a broader government initiative to tighten screening processes for public appointments. The executive noted that some individuals previously convicted or jailed for fraud, or linked to corruption cases, had been proposed by ministers and appointed to other administrative roles. The government stated that individuals with backgrounds compromising responsibility, trust, and suitability for certain functions should not hold positions of special responsibility.

The new criteria for public office candidates now include a more thorough review of their backgrounds and suitability, beyond just professional experience. This aims to prevent those previously convicted of crimes or involved in serious administrative misconduct from returning to positions of responsibility through new appointments, establishing higher standards for each designation.

gq.headline: Vincenzo Alberto Annese signs two-year contract as Nzalang Nacional coach
gq.dek: The Italian coach Vincenzo Alberto Annese officially became the new manager of Equatorial Guinea's national football team, signing a two-year contract on Wednesday, August.
paragraphs: Annese takes over from Juan Micha Obiang, who led the team through a period considered its best in history, including three consecutive Africa Cup of Nations (CAN) qualifications. The new coach faces an immediate challenge to qualify for next year's CAN, with competitive matches beginning next month.

His appointment comes at a demanding time for the Nzalang Nacional, which failed to advance past the group stage in the last CAN. Additionally, the team recently saw the retirement of Emilio Nsue, the all-time leading scorer and captain, and midfielder Pedro Obiang, creating significant gaps in the squad.

Annese expressed satisfaction and commitment during his official presentation at FEGUIFUT in Malabo, acknowledging the scale of the challenge. He emphasized the need for effort to achieve positive results and maintain the Nzalang Nacional's standing in African football amidst these player departures.

gq.headline: Trump administration halts immigrant visa processing globally
gq.dek: The Trump administration has paused interviews and other processing for immigrant visas at US consulates worldwide to train staff on detecting applicants who might use social.
paragraphs: The US State Department announced a global pause on immigrant visa processing, impacting those seeking legal permanent residency through family ties or the visa lottery. This measure does not affect non-immigrant visas for tourism, business, or H1-B skilled workers, which will continue as usual. The department did not specify the duration of this pause.

This suspension is in place to allow for "in-depth training" of diplomatic staff to identify visa applicants who might become a "public charge" or rely on US public assistance reserved for eligible American citizens, according to a State Department spokesperson. The Financial Times reported this information.

Earlier this month, the State Department revoked over 175,000 visas from foreign nationals for violating terms, committing crimes, inciting violence, defrauding Americans, abusing the immigration system, or endangering national security. This new pause aims to ensure visa applicants do not risk becoming a burden on the public system.

gq.headline: Government reforms non-oil revenue collection procedures
gq.dek: The Prime Minister of Equatorial Guinea met with Treasury officials to address inconsistencies and improve the collection of non-oil tax revenues across ministerial departments.
paragraphs: Prime Minister Manuel Osa Nsue Nsua met with Treasury officials in Malabo II to review non-oil revenue reports from ministerial portfolios. The meeting aimed to refine actions for improving tax collection and establish uniform procedures among ministerial departments, the Treasury, and the General Treasury.

The Prime Minister proposed structural reforms, including expanding and strengthening key dependencies within ministries, particularly Economic Section Heads. These actions are considered urgent to rectify ministerial accounts. The official in charge of Administrative Coordination noted that a lack of understanding of the tax law has led to arbitrary issuance of income notes, often not by economic departments, causing chaos in fee amortization.

Treasury officials received direct instructions to implement immediate actions, including drafting a ministerial order detailing measures for economic leadership in ministerial departments. This order will address organizational deficiencies in economic sections, which are identified as the source of many irregularities. Another key aspect will be the purification of accounting entries to identify anomalous or unreal collections and verify document authenticity, aiming to surpass previous collection levels and foster a modern, transparent, and self-sufficient public administration model.

er.headline: Eritrea hosts conference to advance agri-food systems for economic growth
er.dek: The Ministry of Agriculture organized a two-day National Conference on Eritrean Agricultural Studies in Asmara, focusing on sustainable agri-food systems.
paragraphs: Around 300 participants, including ministers, government officials, researchers, academics, and agri-food producers, gathered in Asmara from August 20–21 for the National Conference on Eritrean Agricultural Studies. The Ministry of Agriculture (MoA) organized the event under the theme “Advancing Sustainable Agri-Food Systems for National Economic Growth,” aiming to foster inter-sector solutions for national challenges.

The conference highlighted the importance of collaboration across various sectors, recognizing that improving agri-food systems requires expertise beyond agriculture. Representatives from government institutions, academia, development partners, and producers exchanged knowledge and networked, demonstrating the value of looking beyond institutional boundaries for solutions.

A notable aspect of the conference was the active participation of young professionals and researchers, many holding master’s degrees or higher. This engagement reflects the MoA’s commitment to human-resource development and suggests that such platforms are crucial for building scientific capacity through practice, mentorship, and collaboration.

er.headline: Eritrean Officials Brief Diaspora on National Development and Regional Security
er.dek: Eritrean embassy officials held seminars in Switzerland and Austria to update nationals on the country's security program, social justice principles, and sustainable development.
paragraphs: Eritrean nationals in Switzerland and Austria received updates on national and regional developments from August 16 to 23. Mr. Ismail Mohammed-Nur, Head of Public and Community Affairs at the Eritrean Embassy in Switzerland, conducted seminars in Zug, Schwyz, Schaffhausen, and St. Gallen. He stated that the Government of Eritrea is monitoring developments in the Horn of Africa and collaborating with other nations to prevent potential dangers.

Mr. Ismail also noted the government's efforts to implement its national security program, social justice principles, and sustainable development initiatives to improve citizens' livelihoods. He urged nationals in Switzerland to enhance their awareness and organization to contribute to national development programs, emphasizing the strong position of the Eritrean people due to their unity.

In Vienna, Austria, Mr. Kibreab Tekeste, Eritrea’s Consul General in Frankfurt, and Mr. Teame Haile, Head of Public and Community Affairs at the Eritrean Embassy in Germany, briefed nationals on the homeland's situation, regional and global developments, and the importance of strengthening organizational capacity. They also provided information on consular services and timely responsibilities for nationals abroad.

er.headline: Eritrea plans national celebration for Revolution School's 50th anniversary
er.dek: The Commission of Culture and Sports announced a four-day national celebration from September 17 to 20, marking the 50th anniversary of the Revolution School's establishment.
paragraphs: Eritrea will host a national celebration for the 50th anniversary of the Revolution School from September 17 to 20, under the theme, “Vibrant Commemoration: New Impetus for Nation-Building.” Ambassador Zemede Tekle, Commissioner of Culture and Sports, stated the celebration aims to document the school's history and legacy, highlight the EPLF’s education system, and encourage contributions from Eritrean nationals abroad.

The celebratory events will take place both inside the country and internationally, featuring photo exhibitions, musical concerts, seminars, sports competitions, and a symposium. Official programs are scheduled for Asmara, with regional activities mirroring these events. A photo exhibition will open on September 17 in front of the Central Region Administration building, remaining open for one week.

Further events include a concert and cultural carnival on September 18 along Asmara’s main streets, involving all thirteen sub-zones of the region. Seminars on September 19 at the Expo compound will focus on the Revolution School's role in nationalism and education's contribution to nation-building, alongside a cultural program at Cinema Roma. The celebration will conclude with a symposium and ceremony at the Asmara Palace Hotel on September 20.

er.headline: Eritrean Neuroscientist Promotes National Beauty at Miss Universe
er.dek: Snit Habteab, an Eritrean neuroscientist, Montessori educator, and disability rights advocate, is representing Eritrea at Miss Universe in Vietnam, highlighting the nation's.
paragraphs: Snit Habteab is showcasing Eritrean beauty on the global stage at the Miss Universe competition in Vietnam. Her participation promotes the country's cultural richness and the resilience of Eritrean women, drawing parallels between their endurance and the strength of coral reefs.

The representation emphasizes the concept of “unity in diversity,” likening the intricate beauty of Eritrean women from nine distinct ethnic groups to the varied species within a coral reef. Each group contributes unique aesthetic, cultural, and traditional values to the national identity.

Examples include the classic elegance of Tigrinya women in white cotton gowns, the intricate silver adornments of Tigre and Saho women, the vibrant veils of Rashida women, and the bold beadwork of Afar women. Women from Kunama, Nara, Bilin, and Hedareb ethnic groups are noted for their natural hair textures and earthy bodily ornamentations.

ke.headline: IEBC challenges Gachagua to prove bribery and tender interference claims
ke.dek: The Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) has demanded evidence from Democracy for Citizens Party (DCP) leader Rigathi Gachagua regarding his allegations.
paragraphs: IEBC Chairman Edung Ethekon dismissed claims that politicians influenced the commission's leadership, including allegations that a house was purchased for IEBC Chairperson Erastus Ethekon to sway his decisions. Ethekon urged Gachagua to provide specific evidence, such as the property's location, sale agreements, transfer documents, payment receipts, and details of the seller and purchaser to the Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission (EACC).

The commission also rejected allegations of predetermined awards and political interference in the procurement of electoral technology and ballot papers. Ethekon stated that the procurement processes for the Integrated Elections Management System (IEMS) and ballot papers are in early stages, with no companies yet awarded tenders. These processes are currently halted due to review requests filed with the Public Procurement Administrative Review Board.

Ethekon maintained that tender documents were publicly uploaded on August 11, 2026, and technical specifications are generic and open to all qualified suppliers. He affirmed that all procurement decisions will adhere to Article 227 of the Constitution and the Public Procurement and Asset Disposal Act, emphasizing the commission's independence and focus on its constitutional mandate without political influence.

ke.headline: MPs back passenger charge changes to fund aviation safety and tourism
ke.dek: The National Assembly passed a Bill to channel Air Passenger Service Charge revenue more directly towards aviation safety and tourism promotion.
paragraphs: The National Assembly has approved changes to how revenue from the Air Passenger Service Charge is administered and allocated. The Air Passenger Service Charge (Amendment) Bill, 2026, sponsored by Majority Leader Kimani Ichung’wah, aims to support aviation safety and tourism development. The Bill now moves to the Senate for consideration before it can become law.

The proposed changes seek to strengthen the link between the levy paid by travelers and investment in the sectors that underpin air transport and tourism. Part of the revenue would support institutions responsible for aviation safety and measures to improve the safety and efficiency of air transport operations. This comes as Kenya works to strengthen its aviation infrastructure and regulatory systems.

The legislation also aims to increase support for tourism promotion, a sector heavily dependent on air connectivity. Improved air links are critical for attracting international visitors and facilitating movement within the country. The charge currently stands at Sh600 for domestic routes and US$50 for international journeys, with the Cabinet Secretary able to vary rates.

ke.headline: Kenya records decline in skilled birth attendance, family planning uptake
ke.dek: New data reveals a drop in deliveries by skilled attendants and fewer women using family planning services, highlighting persistent gaps in maternal and newborn healthcare access.
paragraphs: Kenya has seen a decline in skilled birth attendance and family planning uptake, raising concerns about maternal and newborn healthcare. Deliveries conducted by skilled birth attendants fell from 69.77 per cent between April and June 2025 to 65.47 per cent between January and March 2026. The number of women using family planning services also decreased during the same period, according to data presented to editors in Nairobi.

Polycarp Oyoo, Programs Advisor for Maternal and Newborn Health at the International Centre for Reproductive Health Kenya (ICRHK), stated that these figures should prompt closer scrutiny into why women are not consistently accessing antenatal and delivery services. He noted that about 15 mothers are lost daily, with dozens of newborn deaths and stillbirths also recorded each day. Oyoo urged investigation into potential weaknesses within the health system.

Delays contribute significantly to maternal and newborn deaths, with 30 per cent linked to deciding to seek care, 25 per cent to reaching a facility, and 45 per cent occurring after arrival due to untimely or poor care. Only 37 per cent of facilities providing delivery services meet basic Emergency Obstetric and Newborn Care standards, and critical medicine shortages are reported, including 48 per cent lacking magnesium sulphate, 47 per cent lacking benzyl penicillin, and 40 per cent lacking oxytocin.

ke.headline: Kalonzo Musyoka Demands Full Constitutional Implementation in Kenya
ke.dek: Wiper leader Kalonzo Musyoka called for the protection of Kenya's 2010 Constitution, warning against efforts to weaken devolution, democratic institutions, and electoral.
paragraphs: Speaking on the 16th anniversary of the Constitution's promulgation, Kalonzo Musyoka emphasized the supreme law as a shield for citizens and urged vigilance in defending gains since 2010. He highlighted the Constitution's role in transforming governance through devolution, public participation, and stronger protection of fundamental rights.

Musyoka, who served as Vice President when the Constitution was adopted, specifically defended devolution, describing it as a significant gain that brought resources and decision-making closer to citizens. He expressed concern over delays in releasing funds to county governments, arguing that such delays undermine the constitutional promise of devolution and opposed proposals giving the national government greater control over county finances.

Kalonzo also addressed Kenya's electoral system, stating that electoral integrity is critical for stability. He called for an independent, properly funded, and impartial Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) ahead of the 2027 General Election, linking electoral integrity to avoiding a repeat of the 2007 post-election violence that left over 1,000 dead.

ke.headline: Kenyan mothers die from childbirth complications as healthcare falters
ke.dek: Hundreds of mothers in Kenya, including Penina Zawadi, are dying during childbirth due to severe bleeding, obstructed labor, and inadequate medical facilities and transport.
paragraphs: Maternal deaths continue to rise in Kenya, with Kilifi County reporting 532 deaths per 100,000 live births in 2022, significantly higher than the national average of 355. Penina Zawadi died on June 23 after giving birth, following severe bleeding and a delayed transfer from Malindi General Hospital to Kilifi County Referral Hospital, according to her family.

Zawadi's family stated she bled for four hours at Malindi Hospital while awaiting referral to a larger facility an hour away on a potholed road. Her father, Nixon Charo, said they expected a safe birth but circumstances during labor led to her death. Her mother, Esther Bendera, described the extensive bleeding and the doctors' efforts to save her daughter.

The deaths are attributed to shortages of basic medical equipment, inadequate transport for referrals, and insufficient information for pregnant women. While the Kilifi County government reported 81 deaths in the last year and a half as progress, local clinics often lack more than painkillers. Funding cuts from donors have further exacerbated these challenges for vulnerable communities.

za.headline: High Court review delays Danny Jordaan fraud trial until November 2026
za.dek: The fraud case against South African Football Association (SAFA) president Danny Jordaan and co-accused has been postponed to November 27, 2026, pending a High Court decision.
paragraphs: The Specialised Commercial Crimes Court in Palm Ridge postponed the fraud trial involving SAFA president Danny Jordaan and his co-accused to allow the High Court to rule on a review application. This application is linked to an earlier Section 342A application, which permits a court to investigate delays in criminal proceedings. The National Prosecuting Authority (NPA) stated its readiness to proceed with the case, according to communications officer Magaboke Mohlatlole.

Jordaan, former SAFA chief financial officer Grown Hluyo, former journalist and Grit Communications director Trevor Neethling, Grit Communications, and former acting SAFA CEO Russell Paul face multiple charges. These include fraud involving more than R1 million, theft, and conspiracy to commit fraud and theft. The state alleges Jordaan unlawfully signed and backdated a service level agreement with Grit Communications in December 2017, bypassing SAFA's approval processes to benefit his personal image.

Prosecutors also accuse Jordaan of procuring personal security services under the guise of SAFA business operations. Hluyo is alleged to have authorized payments to Grit Communications and a security company despite knowing the agreements were unauthorized by SAFA. Paul is accused of colluding with the others in connection with an allegedly unlawful 2018 service level agreement between SAFA and Grit Communications.

za.headline: Floods in Nepal-Tibet region leave four South Africans missing
za.dek: Four South African nationals are among hundreds of tourists and foreign nationals reported missing after flash floods swept through Nepal’s Rasuwa district near the Tibet border.
paragraphs: Devastating flash floods in Nepal’s Rasuwa district have left at least 95 people dead and more than 403 travelers unaccounted for, including four South African nationals. The disaster struck the mountainous region, a popular route for tourists traveling between Nepal and Tibet, sweeping away a bridge and destroying buildings.

The Nepal Tourism Board confirmed the missing South Africans as part of the 291 foreign nationals among the 384 people still missing. Rescue operations by Nepal’s armed forces and paramilitary units are ongoing, but damaged roads, destroyed bridges, and disrupted communications are hindering efforts to reach affected areas.

The exact cause of the floods remains under investigation, though preliminary reports from Nepal’s Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal suggest an earthquake may have triggered an ice-rock avalanche. The Lhende Khola river, which flows through the affected region, saw a massive surge of water, causing destruction on both the Nepali and Tibetan sides of the border.

za.headline: Scientists investigate Gqeberha fish deaths, warn of industry impact
za.dek: Thousands of dead fish, predominantly sardines, have washed ashore on Gqeberha's beaches, prompting scientists to investigate potential causes and issue warnings about touching.
paragraphs: Thousands of fish, mostly sardines, have washed up dead along Gqeberha's beaches, leading authorities to investigate the cause. Scientists are examining whether pilchard herpesvirus, an algal bloom, or sudden ocean temperature changes are responsible. Nelson Mandela Bay University Professor Nadine Strydom suspects the mortality is linked to the pilchard herpesvirus (PHV) found in the Western Cape earlier this month.

Professor Strydom noted that the number of dead fish visible on beaches is small compared to what lies on the ocean floor, indicating a larger die-off. While other species have been affected, sardines make up most of the deaths. Authorities have advised against collecting or eating the dead fish, though commercially canned sardines are confirmed safe.

The sardine deaths could have significant consequences for the small-scale fishing industry and marine life, according to Professor Strydom. She warned that penguins and other marine animals could face starvation. She also suggested that the government might need to adjust pilchard harvesting quotas to protect the industry, drawing parallels to similar PHV-related mortality events in Australia in the 1990s.

za.headline: Salif Keïta cancels South Africa concerts over 'xenophobic violence'
za.dek: Malian musician Salif Keïta has canceled all future South African performances, citing recent waves of xenophobic violence across the country.
paragraphs: World-famous Malian musician Salif Keïta has canceled his upcoming South African concerts, including a festival performance next month, due to what he described as "xenophobic violence." Keïta stated that the xenophobia did not "match the South Africa I know," according to BBC Africa.

This decision follows a wave of protests in South Africa demanding that undocumented migrants leave the country, with an unofficial deadline set for September 30. Tens of thousands of Africans have voluntarily repatriated in recent months, with some reporting intimidation and attacks.

While the South African government has been cracking down on illegal immigration, it has also stated that individuals who have taken the law into their own hands have been arrested. South Africa, as Africa's wealthiest nation, has historically attracted migrants seeking better economic opportunities, but illegal immigration has become a contentious political issue, with protesters accusing migrants of straining public services and involvement in crime.

za.headline: South Africa shifts education to meet job market demands
za.dek: South Africa is transitioning from pre-2009 occupational qualifications to a new system that links skills directly to employment, self-employment, entrepreneurship, and lifelong.
paragraphs: South Africa is moving to update its education system to better prepare its workforce for current and future economic needs, according to Dr. Makhapa Makhafola, chairperson of the Ministerial Technical Task Team and COO for the South African Qualifications Authority. This shift aims to address the country's unemployment crisis by focusing on occupational qualifications instead of outdated credentials.

The change comes as South Africa's unemployment figures continue to rise. The official unemployment rate increased from 32.7% in the first quarter to 33.6% in the second quarter, with 345,000 more people becoming unemployed, bringing the total to 8.5 million, according to Stats SA's Quarterly Labour Force Survey (QLFS).

Youth unemployment is particularly high, increasing by 1.5 percentage points to 47.4%, with five million young people now unemployed. This represents an increase of 264,000 young people without jobs, while the number of employed young people decreased by 40,000 to 5.6 million in the last quarter.
