ng.headline: President Tinubu orders comprehensive reform of Nigerian football after NFF resignations
ng.dek: President Bola Tinubu has directed a complete overhaul of Nigerian football, hours after the Nigeria Football Federation's leadership resigned due to team failures.
paragraphs: President Bola Tinubu has ordered a comprehensive reform of Nigerian football, citing the national teams' repeated failures to qualify for major international competitions. This directive came on Thursday, following the resignations of Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) President Ibrahim Musa Gusau, General Secretary Mohammed Sanusi, and other Executive Committee members.

The NFF confirmed the mass resignations, stating that Gusau's decision aimed to facilitate an orderly reform process to address long-standing institutional, governance, and developmental issues. Bayo Onanuga, Special Adviser to the President on Information and Strategy, announced the presidential order, noting Tinubu's view that structural weaknesses within the system have caused the decline.

President Tinubu emphasized that the reform must strengthen governance, administration, stakeholder representation, development pathways, domestic competitions, and accountability across Nigerian football. He highlighted that despite significant public support and investment, football in Nigeria has struggled due to these systemic deficits, contrasting it with progress seen in other sports after the restructuring of the sports sector.

ng.headline: First Lady's Initiative Supports 1,638 Families of Fallen Police Officers
ng.dek: The Renewed Hope Initiative (RHI) provided financial aid to 1,638 families of police officers who died in the line of duty since President Bola Tinubu’s administration began.
paragraphs: The Renewed Hope Initiative (RHI) Social Investment Programme, led by First Lady Senator Oluremi Tinubu, delivered financial support to 1,638 families of police officers who lost their lives while serving. This intervention, the second edition of the initiative, specifically targets families of security personnel who died in the line of duty since the current administration commenced.

The financial empowerment packages, presented at the Presidential Villa in Abuja, aim to help these families rebuild their livelihoods and care for their dependents. Inspector-General of Police, IGP Olatunji Rilwan Disu, attended the ceremony and expressed appreciation for the gesture, describing it as a demonstration of national gratitude.

The event also saw the attendance of the wife of the Vice President, Hajia Nana Shettima, the wife of the Senate President, Mrs Ekaette Unoma Akpabio, service chiefs, and the President of the Police Officers’ Wives Association (POWA). The IGP assured the bereaved families that the sacrifices of their loved ones would not be forgotten and affirmed the police force's commitment to personnel welfare.

paragraphs: Nigeria's financial future is heavily influenced by its young population, with nearly three-quarters of citizens under the age of 24, according to the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). This demographic reality prompts questions about the preparedness of young Nigerians to engage in investment activities and build long-term wealth.

The SEC's statistics underscore the importance of equipping this large youth demographic with the necessary knowledge, access, and discipline for investing. The financial sector faces the challenge of ensuring that this significant portion of the population can actively participate in and benefit from the country's economic growth.

A decade of fund returns is being examined to understand how it can inform young Nigerians about starting early in investment. This analysis aims to provide practical insights into wealth creation for a population segment that will largely shape the nation's economic landscape in the coming years.

Sudanese authorities and human rights organizations have accused the RSF of targeting civilian infrastructure during this conflict.

et.headline: Minibus-Excavator Crash Kills Six in Addis Ababa
et.dek: A traffic accident involving a minibus taxi and an excavator in Addis Ababa's Bole Subcity claimed the lives of at least six people on Monday, according to police.
paragraphs: Six people died in a traffic accident in Addis Ababa on Monday when an excavator's bucket fell onto a moving minibus taxi, the Addis Ababa Police reported. The incident, which occurred in the morning of August 24, also left the minibus driver and several other passengers with serious or minor injuries, requiring medical treatment at nearby health facilities.

The police have launched an investigation to determine the exact cause of the accident. This incident is part of a series of deadly traffic accidents in Ethiopia, which authorities often link to factors such as reckless driving, weak law enforcement, and poor vehicle conditions.

Experts are calling for stricter safety enforcement, thorough vehicle inspections, and more rigorous licensing systems to prevent future tragedies. These calls come as vehicle numbers rise in the East African nation, alongside its growing economy and expanding middle class.

et.headline: WHO, AU Leaders Call for African Health Sovereignty
et.dek: Leaders from the World Health Organization and African Union convened in Addis Ababa to advocate for Africa-led health sovereignty, aiming to reduce reliance on external.
paragraphs: The 76th Session of the WHO Regional Committee for Africa, held in Addis Ababa, brought together African health ministers and leaders to discuss the continent's health future. Mohamed Yakub Janabi, WHO regional director for Africa, stated that the session will review Africa’s determination to shape its own health future and make decisions to improve health services across the continent.

The initiative seeks to reduce the nearly seven billion U.S. dollars Africa spends annually on referring patients abroad. Janabi emphasized strengthening Africa’s centers of excellence and connecting African patients to African expertise to keep investments working for the continent. AU Commission Chairperson Mahmoud Ali Youssouf highlighted Africa's efforts to achieve health sovereignty through vaccine production and increased budget allocations.

Ethiopian President Taye Atske Selassie, the guest of honor, noted that climate change and conflict are exerting pressure on African communities, disrupting health services and displacing populations. He suggested these challenges present an opportunity for Africa to strengthen its collective voice, deepen regional cooperation, and assume full ownership of its health architecture. The session is set to endorse regional health policies and strategies to improve health outcomes.

gh.headline: AI strategy risks GH¢500bn target, warns MyJoyOnline
gh.dek: Ghana's new National Artificial Intelligence Strategy, aiming to inject GHc500 billion into the economy, faces potential setbacks from AI-driven job displacement and foreign.
paragraphs: A recent analysis by MyJoyOnline highlights that Ghana's National Artificial Intelligence Strategy (2025–2035) may inadvertently undermine its own goal of adding GHc500 billion to the national economy. The report suggests that while AI is seen as an efficiency booster, the aggressive replacement of human workers with automated software could lead to an 'AI Layoff Trap,' reducing consumer spending.

The analysis points out that AI displacement differs from past industrial revolutions by directly targeting routine cognitive tasks, such as basic legal research, entry-level bookkeeping, and customer service. These roles are crucial entry points for thousands of tertiary graduates entering Ghana's job market annually, and their elimination creates 'Diamond-Shaped Organizations' with fewer junior positions.

MyJoyOnline identifies three critical blindspots in the strategy: a potential collapse in Pay-As-You-Earn (PAYE) income tax revenue as white-collar workers are replaced, invisible foreign exchange capital flight due to recurring payments for foreign-owned AI models in US Dollars, and the erosion of domestic purchasing power, which threatens consumer-facing businesses.

gh.headline: Ghana Maritime Authority partners local leaders to improve inland water safety
gh.dek: The Ghana Maritime Authority is collaborating with Upper West Assemblies and traditional leaders to enforce new safety measures on the Black Volta, aiming to prevent recurring.
paragraphs: The Ghana Maritime Authority (GMA) has initiated a partnership with Municipal and District Chief Executives, security heads, traditional authorities, and boat operators in the Upper West Region. This collaboration, part of the GMA’s Life Jackets for Safety and Livelihoods Initiative, seeks to build grassroots consensus and enforce a strict “No Life Jacket, No Boarding” policy to eliminate fatal capsize incidents on inland waterways.

Director-General Naval Captain (Rtd) Dr. Kamal-Deen Ali stated that enhancing inland water safety is a top priority, citing the tragic loss of seven students in a disaster at Dikpe last year. The GMA has established a Black Volta Coordination Office in Wa and trained 200 Inland Water Safety Guards, with a substantial number deployed to the Upper West Region to monitor riverbanks and ensure passenger compliance.

To address the leading causes of drowning, identified as non-compliance and lack of standard life jackets, the GMA is offering subsidized life jackets at GH₵250 each, or GH₵230 for bulk community purchases, down from over GH₵400. They also plan to expand the safety guard force from 200 to over 350 personnel and have removed 26,448 submerged tree stumps nationwide since 2019 to clear navigational paths.

gh.headline: World Bank confirms 56.4% of Ghanaians remain in poverty despite growth
gh.dek: New findings from the World Bank indicate that over half of Ghana's population lives in poverty, highlighting a disconnect between economic growth and household living conditions.
paragraphs: The World Bank's 10th Ghana Economic Update, released in August 2026, reports that 56.4% of Ghanaians are still in poverty. This figure comes despite strong economic growth in 2025, significant disinflation, and improved macroeconomic indicators. The Bank's Division Director for Ghana, Liberia, and Sierra Leone noted that growth is concentrated in sectors with limited job creation capacity, and spatial disparities are widening.

The Africa Policy Lens (APL) stated that these World Bank findings validate its April 2026 Ghana Wellbeing Tracker report. That report concluded Ghana was “stabilising but not yet thriving,” with its Ghana Wellbeing Index (GWI) at 58.5 out of 100, placing the country in the fragile-to-neutral range.

APL's Policy Brief No. 1 for August 2026 emphasized that both assessments, using different methodologies, agree that macroeconomic recovery has outpaced household economic recovery. This convergence reinforces the policy challenge of achieving “recovery without broad-based welfare gains,” according to APL, and highlights the need for stabilization to translate into jobs and improved living standards.

gh.headline: IEA clarifies US$1.7bn gold program loss as accounting issue
gh.dek: The Institute of Economic Affairs (IEA) states that a significant portion of the reported US$1.7 billion loss in Ghana's gold purchase program is due to accounting and valuation.
paragraphs: The Institute of Economic Affairs (IEA) announced that the reported US$1.7 billion loss from the Bank of Ghana’s Domestic Gold Purchase Programme is largely an accounting issue, not an actual loss to the economy. Professor Alexander Bilson-Darku, Director of Research at the IEA, speaking at their assessment of the 2026 mid-year budget review in Accra on Wednesday, urged for proper disaggregation of the figure before drawing conclusions.

Professor Bilson-Darku explained that the first two components of the reported loss represent payments from the central bank to the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) for gold purchased and exported. He noted these payments constitute revenue for GoldBod, a state institution, making it a cost for the central bank but not a loss to the state as a whole.

The most significant part, accounting for almost 90 per cent of the US$1.7 billion, stems from the Bank of Ghana's valuation method. This involves converting dollar proceeds into cedis on the central bank's books using reference rates that can differ from prevailing foreign exchange rates, creating a book issue rather than a cash loss for Ghana.

cd.dek: The Sustainable Agriculture Pre-Retirement and Retirement Program (PROPRAD) launched in Kinshasa to offer professional retraining and economic empowerment through farming.
paragraphs: A new initiative aims to help individuals nearing the end of their professional careers in the DR Congo prepare for retirement or career change through agricultural entrepreneurship. The Sustainable Agriculture Pre-Retirement and Retirement Program (PROPRAD) was launched on August eight in Kinshasa by the Bilanga ya Betu Agricultural Cooperative, in collaboration with the Grouping for Food Self-Sufficiency and Biodiversity (RATALBI).

The program's stated ambition is to use agricultural entrepreneurship as a means to gradually prepare for retirement, promote professional retraining, and foster economic empowerment. It encompasses various agricultural activities such as market gardening, livestock farming, fish farming, and agricultural processing, offering multiple possibilities for participants.

PROPRAD also includes provisions for savings mechanisms, financing, support, and insurance, along with connecting beneficiaries to various partners. cd.headline: Ituri Education Director Confirms School Reopening Despite Ebola
cd.dek: Schools in Ituri province will resume classes on September one, 2026, as planned, despite ongoing concerns about the Ebola epidemic.
paragraphs: The 2026-2027 school year will begin on September one in Ituri province, confirmed Yvon Muke Abwasele, director of the Ituri I educational province, on Wednesday, August twenty-six. This decision comes amidst persistent anxieties among parents regarding the health safety of students.

Provincial education authorities have implemented measures to secure school environments, according to Abwasele. School principals have received training and awareness sessions to enforce barrier measures against Ebola. Necessary kits and exercise books for distance learning are also available to address potential emergencies.

Abwasele emphasized that the provincial education system is prepared for the reopening, stating that distance learning would be activated for any school experiencing a resurgence of cases. Parents in Ituri remain divided, balancing financial constraints with fears of their children's exposure to the virus, and are requesting enhanced sanitary provisions in all schools.

cd.headline: Mukwege condemns M23 academic appointments, school closures
cd.dek: Nobel Peace Prize laureate Dr. Denis Mukwege denounced the M23's imposition of academic authorities and Kinshasa's suspension of academic activities in occupied territories.
paragraphs: Dr. Denis Mukwege, a Nobel Peace Prize laureate, condemned the armed movements AFC/M23/RDF for appointing new academic authorities in higher education institutions within occupied zones. He also criticized the Kinshasa regime's decision to suspend academic activities in these areas, as stated in a communiqué on Wednesday, August twenty-sixth.

Mukwege highlighted that the closure of universities, following restrictions on airports, banks, humanitarian aid, and population movement, further tightens the grip on twelve million Congolese citizens in North and South Kivu. He described denying young people the opportunity to learn and train as an unacceptable "red line."

The doctor called on all state and non-state actors involved in resolving the crisis to prioritize the education of Congolese children. He demanded an end to military interference in educational management and a secure resumption of classes across the entire territory, including occupied areas, emphasizing that youth's future should not be a political bargaining chip.

tz.headline: CCM expels former Vice President Nchimbi for party rule violations
tz.dek: Tanzania's ruling Chama Cha Mapinduzi (CCM) party expelled Emmanuel Nchimbi a day after his resignation, citing conduct that violated party rules and regulations.
paragraphs: The Chama Cha Mapinduzi (CCM) party announced the expulsion of former Vice President Emmanuel Nchimbi on August 26, 2026. This decision came a day after Nchimbi publicly resigned from his position. Party General Secretary Asha Rose Migiro stated that Nchimbi's expulsion was due to conduct that violated the party's rules concerning discipline and ethics, a matter discussed and resolved by both the Central Committee and the National Executive Committee.

Migiro informed the press at approximately 10:30 pm that the National Executive Committee unanimously passed a resolution to remove Nchimbi from membership. The expulsion is effective immediately, meaning Nchimbi is no longer a member of the Chama Cha Mapinduzi. This action follows Nchimbi's resignation, which was announced through a dormant personal account, a day before parliament was scheduled to resume its session.

Nchimbi's resignation and subsequent expulsion occur amidst speculation of a falling-out with President Samia Suluhu Hassan, though neither side has confirmed this. His advocacy for a new constitution and his stance on reform and justice are seen by some as contributing factors to the rift. Nchimbi was considered a reformer within the ruling party, having previously championed greater tolerance towards political opponents and activists.

tz.headline: Prosecution cross-examines CHADEMA chairperson Lissu in treason trial
tz.dek: State attorneys questioned Tundu Lissu on his April 3, 2025 speech and its online publication after he concluded his defense in the High Court.
paragraphs: The prosecution began cross-examining CHADEMA chairperson Tundu Lissu on Wednesday in Dar es Salaam, focusing on remarks he made in an April 3, 2025 speech and its subsequent online publication. State Attorney Nassoro Katuga pressed Lissu on whether he intended his speech to reach the public and if he controlled its streaming by Jambo TV. Lissu confirmed he wanted the speech to reach citizens, stating it contained "very important information," but denied controlling the publication, attributing that decision to a Jambo TV employee.

The questioning followed a two-day pause in proceedings, with Lissu having delivered his final defense submissions earlier on Wednesday. Lissu, a lawyer and CHADEMA chair, acknowledged his legal training and lack of immunity. He confirmed making the words attributed to him, including references to "kukinukisha," "mobilising rebellion," and "stopping the election," but argued these phrases were taken out of context from a longer speech.

The exchange became pointed when Lissu stated he had no obligation to provide documentary proof for awards and international bodies he cited in his defense, unless challenged by the prosecution. Katuga also challenged Lissu's position that citizens can lawfully oppose election laws and government decisions through public mobilization, a significant part of the cross-examination.

tz.headline: Tanzania hosts ADDI delegation at National Museum

Ambassador Arikana Chihombori-Quao from Zimbabwe, founder and president of ADDI, led the delegation. She urged Africans to unite, cooperate, and maintain peace, emphasizing the importance of unity in protecting and developing Africa's heritage.

Dr. Aloyce Mwambwiga, Chief Curator of the National Museum and House of Culture, encouraged both local citizens and international visitors to explore the National Museum to learn more about Tanzania's history, culture, and heritage. This visit is part of efforts to promote cultural diplomacy and showcase Tanzania through its historical and cultural legacy to both domestic and international guests.

tz.headline: Tanzanian Energy Ministry Intervenes in Ntorya Gas Dispute, Secures Production Pledge
tz.dek: Tanzanian energy officials met with gas developers APT and Ndovu Resources following a dispute notice, aiming to streamline operations and meet the December 2026 production.
paragraphs: The Ministry of Energy's Permanent Secretary, Dr. James Mataragio, convened a meeting on August 26, 2026, with key stakeholders in the Ntorya Gas Development, including ARA Petroleum Tanzania Limited (APT), Ndovu Resources Limited, the Tanzania Petroleum Development Corporation (TPDC), and the Petroleum Upstream Regulatory Authority (PURA). This intervention followed a notice of dispute issued by Ndovu Resources on August 21, 2026, alleging breaches by APT of its obligations under the Farmout Agreement and Joint Operating Agreement.

Ndovu Resources' dispute notice specifically cited APT's failure to implement the approved 2026 Work Programme and Budget (2026 WP&B), which included drilling the CH-1 well. Instead, APT reportedly pursued alternative programs that delayed the drilling and lacked the same firm commitment. These proposed changes were not approved by the Joint Venture, TPDC, or PURA, leading to material delays and minimal work during 2026.

Following the ministry's meeting, APT Chief Executive Officer Dr. Salman Al Shidi pledged to ensure the company fulfills its responsibilities and completes the necessary steps to commence gas production by the revised target of December 2026. The Ntorya gas field, located in the Ruvuma Basin, holds an estimated 1.6 trillion cubic feet of natural gas, with APT owning 75 percent and Ndovu 25 percent of the project.

tz.headline: Tanzania proposes sugar law changes to boost industry control and investment
tz.dek: The government introduced a bill to parliament today that seeks to amend the Sugar Industry Act, Chapter 251, to improve product quality and increase investment.
paragraphs: The Tanzanian government has submitted the Agricultural Laws (Amendments) Act, 2026, to parliament, proposing changes to four laws, including the Sugar Industry Act. Minister of Agriculture Daniel Chongolo presented the bill, stating that the amendments aim to expand the scope of controlled sugar products and enhance their quality.

Key proposed changes include requiring registration for sugar factories based on the intended use of the produced sugar. Additionally, the bill seeks to allow refined and raw sugar imports by existing raw sugar processing plants for industrial use, aiming to increase control and promote investment in the sector.

Further amendments separate the implementation agreement from the import license for sugar, reinforcing the agreement as a tool for regulating producers and raw sugar imports for industrial use. The bill also expands the scope of individuals allowed to repackage domestically produced sugar in quantities not exceeding 100 grams, including those not registered as producers, to strengthen control over repackaging activities and protect sugar quality and standards.

ma.headline: Spain finds no evidence Morocco linked to Ceuta migrant influx
ma.dek: Spain's government stated there is no evidence connecting Morocco to the mass arrival of approximately 70,000 migrants in Ceuta on July 30 and 31.
paragraphs: Spain's Justice Minister Félix Bolaños confirmed that there is no evidence linking Morocco to the mass entry of migrants into Ceuta, rejecting opposition claims of Rabat's involvement. Bolaños told the Spanish parliament’s Joint National Security Committee that Spain had no prior or precise information regarding the scale of the influx, which saw about 70,000 people enter the Spanish enclave.

Bolaños defended Spain's relationship with Morocco, describing it as based on cooperation and good neighborliness, and accused some opposition politicians of spreading "lies" and "doubts" without evidence. He also noted that neither the Spanish nor Moroccan governments had raised the issue of sovereignty over Ceuta and Melilla during their bilateral contacts.

Regarding migrant minors, Bolaños stated that Morocco has expressed willingness to cooperate on returns and family reunification, though these procedures are complex and must comply with Spanish legal safeguards. He emphasized that Spain's migration policy, partly due to cooperation with countries like Morocco, is achieving better results in controlling irregular migration than other European countries.

ma.headline: Moroccan security agencies deny cyberattack on databases
ma.dek: Morocco's General Directorate of National Security (DGSN) and the General Directorate for Territorial Surveillance (DGST) stated their information systems remain secure, refuting.
paragraphs: Moroccan security authorities on Thursday denied reports of a cyberattack on their information systems or security databases. The DGSN-DGST joint pole stated that recently circulated personal data did not originate from a breach of their systems, which are protected by the highest standards of cybersecurity.

The authorities clarified that the personal data published online consisted of old information obtained from databases operated by insurance companies and organizations providing health and social coverage. They also warned against the circulation of fabricated photographs falsely presented as images of security personnel and altered documents allegedly from Moroccan security services.

The DGSN-DGST pole noted that some fake material uses uniforms and military ranks not present in Morocco and contains incorrect visual identities and linguistic errors. Security investigations into the circulation of this data and fabricated material will continue under the supervision of competent authorities.

ma.headline: Morocco coach Ouahbi tours Europe to assess players for AFCON qualifiers
ma.dek: Coach Mohamed Ouahbi will visit several European countries in early September to evaluate Moroccan international players before finalizing his squad for the upcoming Africa Cup.
paragraphs: Morocco's national football team coach, Mohamed Ouahbi, will travel to Europe in the first week of September to meet with players ahead of the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying matches. The tour aims to assess the physical and technical condition of Moroccan internationals, particularly those who recently moved clubs, are returning from injuries, or have caught the technical staff's attention.

Ouahbi's itinerary includes meetings with established players like Nayef Aguerd and Abdessamad Ezzalzouli, whose fitness is crucial for the team. He will also check on young talents such as Abdullah Ouazane from Ajax and Soufiane Farsi from Schalke, as part of efforts to get an up-to-date assessment of European-based players before naming his final squad.

The Confederation of African Football has scheduled Morocco's initial two qualifying matches. The Atlas Lions will host Gabon on September 25 at Prince Moulay Abdellah Stadium in Rabat, with a 7 p.m. GMT kickoff. They will then travel to South Africa to play Lesotho on September 29, with the match starting at 1 p.m. GMT at Toyota Stadium in Bloemfontein.

The tour aims to assess the physical and technical condition of Moroccan internationals, particularly those who recently moved clubs, are returning from injuries, or have caught the technical staff's attention.

Ouahbi's itinerary includes meetings with established players like Nayef Aguerd and Abdessamad Ezzalzouli, whose fitness is crucial for the team. He will also check on young talents such as Abdullah Ouazane from Ajax and Soufiane Farsi from Schalke, as part of efforts to get an up-to-date assessment of European-based players before naming his final squad.

The Confederation of African Football has scheduled Morocco's initial two qualifying matches. The Atlas Lions will host Gabon on September 25 at Prince Moulay Abdellah Stadium in Rabat, with a 7 p.m. GMT kickoff. They will then travel to South Africa to play Lesotho on September 29, with the match starting at 1 p.m. GMT at Toyota Stadium in Bloemfontein.

ug.headline: WHO declares Uganda Ebola-free, hands over mobile lab
ug.dek: The World Health Organization officially declared Uganda free of Ebola after the country completed 42 days without a new confirmed case, a global standard for ending outbreaks.
paragraphs: Uganda has been declared Ebola-free by the World Health Organization (WHO) following a 42-day period without any new confirmed cases, a global standard for declaring an outbreak over. This declaration, made by Dr. Kasonde Mwinga, the WHO Representative in Uganda, provides additional assurance that no transmission chains linked to the imported case in May were missed.

The Ministry of Health had previously declared the country Ebola-free almost a month earlier, based on an assessment of no active transmission. Dr. Diana Atwine, Permanent Secretary in the Ministry of Health, stated that this official declaration should prompt countries that imposed travel restrictions on Uganda to lift them, as these measures have impacted the economy.

Despite the declaration, the Ministry of Health will maintain surveillance, including monitoring deaths and screening travelers, especially at borders, due to ongoing Ebola transmission in the Democratic Republic of Congo. WHO also handed over a truck-mounted mobile laboratory, valued at 500,000 US dollars and donated by the African Development Bank, to strengthen Uganda's preparedness for public health emergencies.

ug.headline: Kassanda Police Investigate Death of Theft Suspect After Mob Attack
ug.dek: Police in Kassanda District have opened a murder investigation after Derrick Kasumba, a 30-year-old burglary and theft suspect, died following a mob assault shortly.
paragraphs: Derrick Kasumba, also known as Kalevu, died on August 23, 2026, after being intercepted and assaulted by a mob in Lwenyange Village. Kasumba had escaped from Manyogaseka Sub-county Police Station at approximately 9 am while being escorted to the toilet, according to Wamala Region Police spokesperson SSP Lameck Kigozi.

Police Constable Aaron Nalyanya, who was guarding Kasumba, reportedly failed to prevent his escape. About an hour later, police received information that Kasumba was being assaulted by a mob. PC Nalyanya was instructed to rescue and re-arrest him, finding the mob assaulting Kasumba before they fled.

Kasumba was transported back to the police station, but his condition worsened, and he was evacuated to Kyansaswa Health Centre III, where he was pronounced dead about 40 minutes after arrival. Police are now investigating the murder, working to identify and arrest members of the mob, and examining the circumstances of Kasumba's escape and death.

ug.headline: Gen. Muhoozi, Tyrese Gibson discuss Uganda tourism and investment
ug.dek: General Muhoozi Kainerugaba and American actor Tyrese Gibson met in Entebbe to explore promoting Uganda as a tourism and investment destination.
paragraphs: Chief of Defence Forces, Gen. Muhoozi Kainerugaba, held discussions with American actor and musician Tyrese Gibson in Entebbe to promote Uganda's tourism and investment opportunities. The meeting focused on leveraging Uganda's natural resources, cultural heritage, and growing creative economy to attract international attention and partnerships. Gibson's visit comes as Uganda aims to position tourism and creative arts as key contributors to economic growth.

The discussions explored using global entertainment personalities to showcase Uganda's tourism potential and strengthen ties between its creative industry and international networks. This includes creating opportunities for local filmmakers, actors, musicians, and technicians to gain exposure, while attracting productions and investments. Uganda possesses diverse attractions, including mountain gorillas, wildlife, forests, lakes, and rivers.

Beyond tourism, the engagement also touched on the creative industry's role in youth empowerment, providing avenues for skills development, employment, and entrepreneurship for Uganda's large, youthful population. Gibson also met with President Yoweri Kaguta Museveni to discuss creative arts, tourism, and promoting Africa's shared heritage, aiming to strengthen Uganda's film and entertainment industry as an economic driver.

ug.headline: Police arrest former Sky Pins director for alleged recruitment fraud
ug.dek: Christian Asiimwe, known as Don Chris, was arrested in Zana for allegedly defrauding over 500 job seekers of up to Shs 1.75 billion.
paragraphs: Police arrested Christian Asiimwe, also known as Don Chris, a former director of the defunct labour recruitment company Sky Pins, on Thursday, August 27, 2026. He faces allegations of obtaining money by false pretenses and fraudulent labour recruitment. Asiimwe was apprehended at a bar in Zana, Makindye-Ssabagabo Municipality, Wakiso District, following a nationwide manhunt that began in June 2025.

Asiimwe is accused of collecting between Shs 5 million and Shs 10 million from each of more than 500 alleged victims between 2022 and 2025. He allegedly promised them jobs abroad in countries like Canada, the United Kingdom, Qatar, and Dubai, for roles such as waiters, cleaners, and caregivers. The total amount collected from victims is estimated to be between Shs 1.4 billion and Shs 1.75 billion.

Investigations by the Criminal Investigations Directorate (CID) intensified after 85 job seekers petitioned the state minister for Youth and Children Affairs in June 2025. Sky Pins had advertised extensively, promising employment on credit with an upfront payment. None of the applicants reportedly traveled as promised, and the company's offices were found abandoned. Asiimwe is currently in police custody, and authorities urge caution when dealing with recruitment companies.

ug.headline: Uganda targets mortgage financing to boost tenfold economic growth
ug.dek: Uganda's ambition to increase its economy from US$50 billion to US$500 billion by 2040 relies on stronger financial systems, with mortgage financing identified as a key mechanism.
paragraphs: Uganda aims to leverage mortgage financing to achieve its ambitious goal of tenfold economic growth by 2040, as highlighted by Andrew Musanje. The country's housing sector, which currently contributes about 11 percent to GDP, faces a deficit of 2.4 million units, with only about 60,000 units constructed annually against an estimated demand of 200,000.

Mortgage loans account for less than 1 percent of Uganda's GDP, a figure significantly lower than many emerging economies. This underdevelopment in housing finance means many Ugandans rely on personal savings to build homes, often resulting in substandard structures and tying up household capital for years, according to Musanje.

The National Development Plan IV recognizes affordable housing as crucial for Uganda's transformation. Increased mortgage financing could accelerate construction, create jobs across various sectors like manufacturing and banking, and allow households to convert future income into productive investments, thereby fostering asset accumulation and financial security.

zw.headline: RIDA Official Arrested, Charged in Lake Kariba Ferry Disaster
zw.dek: Ignatius Chiome, the Kariba Rural Infrastructure Development Agency (RIDA) District Coordinator, faces culpable homicide charges following the capsizing of the Mbuya Nehanda ferry.
paragraphs: Ignatius Chiome, 49, the Kariba Rural Infrastructure Development Agency (RIDA) District Coordinator, has been arrested and charged with culpable homicide in connection with the Lake Kariba ferry disaster. The arrest comes two weeks after the RIDA-operated Mbuya Nehanda ferry capsized on August eleven, resulting in the deaths of ninety-seven people. Chiome appeared in court and was remanded in custody, according to Zimbabwe Republic Police spokesperson Commissioner Paul Nyathi.

The ferry, which was traveling from Kariba towards Chalala, had an authorized capacity of ninety passengers but was reportedly carrying significantly more. Authorities later acknowledged the vessel was severely overloaded when it encountered rough conditions on the lake. This incident marks Zimbabwe's worst recorded maritime disaster, with seventy-seven people rescued from the tragedy.

The Mbuya Nehanda ferry served as a vital transport link for remote communities around Chalala, enabling residents to move people, fish, and other goods. Investigations into the disaster are ongoing, and Chiome has not yet entered a plea to the culpable homicide charge.

zw.headline: Zimbabwe proposes US$1 million quarterly payment for SAA debt
zw.dek: Zimbabwe has suggested paying US$1 million every three months to settle a debt of over US$50 million owed to South African Airways (SAA), accumulated since 2020.
paragraphs: Zimbabwe's government has proposed a payment plan of US$1 million per quarter to address its outstanding debt to South African Airways (SAA), which totals over US$50 million. This debt stems from SAA ticket sales for flights between Johannesburg, Harare, and Victoria Falls, and has been accruing since 2020. The proposal, made in 2024, was rejected by SAA officials who considered the repayment timeline of over 16 years to be too long.

The South African Department of International Relations was scheduled to appear before Parliament on Tuesday to explain its efforts to recover these funds. SAA is owed a total of R1.4 billion by various countries, with Zimbabwe's debt forming the bulk of this amount. Former SAA chief financial officer Lindsay Olitzski stated that no funds had been received under the proposed plan.

Discussions regarding the debt have occurred between President Cyril Ramaphosa of South Africa and his Zimbabwean counterpart, Emmerson Mnangagwa, according to Newzroom Afrika. Despite these high-level talks and the long-standing nature of the debt, a business and finance writer, Ntokozo Khumalo, noted that six or so years later, nothing has been paid.

zw.headline: Mutapa awards US$41 million York-Sandawana road contract
zw.dek: Mutapa Energy Resources has appointed three contractors to upgrade and tar a 52-kilometre road linking York and Sandawana in Mberengwa, as the lithium miner develops.
paragraphs: Mutapa Energy Resources (MER) has awarded a US$41 million contract to three contractors for upgrading and tarring a 52-kilometre road between York and Sandawana in Mberengwa. Fossil, Masimba, and Shumba Mhazi Group (SM Projects) received different sections of the road and have been given mobilisation payments, according to MER chief executive officer Innocent Rukweza. Masimba will construct the Mutsime Bridge and work on a 17-kilometre section.

The road upgrade is part of MER's infrastructure development around its operations, including a planned US$300 million lithium concentrator plant at Sandawana, targeted for commissioning by November 2027. The project also involves relocating 104 families, with MER building seven demonstration houses before rolling out construction of the remaining homes. Each household will receive a four-roomed house, kitchen, and ablution facilities at an estimated cost of US$28 000.

MER aims to finalise all 104 houses by the end of September, with relocation of affected families to follow. More than 52 graves within the proposed plant site are expected to be exhumed around September 1, pending burial orders. The company has generated over US$80 million from ore deliveries to the Gwanda lithium plant this year and targets revenue of between US$100 million and US$140 million.

zw.headline: Blue Ribbon, 23 other millers halt Bulawayo operations over maize shortage
zw.dek: Twenty-four milling companies in Bulawayo have ceased operations due to a lack of locally produced maize, impacting consistent maize meal production in the southern region.
paragraphs: Blue Ribbon Industries and 23 other medium and small-scale millers have shut down their grain milling operations in Bulawayo, according to a letter sent to government ministries by Major (Rtd) David Moyo, chairperson of the Grain Millers Association Southern Region. The closures are attributed to a significant decline in locally produced maize available for commercial milling, affecting Matebeleland North, Matebeleland South, and Bulawayo.

The shortage has prevented millers from maintaining consistent production levels and building adequate maize reserves. Moyo's circular to the Ministry of Industry, the Ministry of Agriculture, and Bulawayo’s Minister of State stated that local maize supplies have declined, with some maize also infested by insects, increasing operational costs for millers.

Moyo also cited challenges with Statutory Instrument (SI) 87 of 2025, which set a US$40/MT price for local maize and requires upfront payment for imported maize, making it inaccessible on 30 to 60-day payment terms. He expressed concern that the Ministry of Agriculture is not prioritizing the southern region, a situation he described as a replay of the previous year.

zw.headline: Sinomine secures additional lithium export quota from Zimbabwe
zw.dek: Sinomine Resource Group has obtained an export quota for an additional 300 000 metric tonnes of lithium concentrate from Zimbabwe, as announced by the company.
paragraphs: Sinomine Resource Group has secured an additional export quota for 300 000 metric tonnes of lithium concentrate from Zimbabwe, according to the company. This follows an initial quota of 200 000 tonnes granted in April, with the new quota approved in July. Zimbabwe, Africa’s top producer of battery metal lithium, introduced export quotas in April after temporarily halting concentrate shipments in February due to alleged malpractice and leakages.

The Chinese company, which operates the Bikita lithium mine, stated in a half-year report seen by Reuters that the supply of lithium concentrate from Bikita has returned to normal after the February to April stoppages. This supply is sufficient to meet the raw material requirements of its smelting operations in China. Zimbabwe has been pushing mining firms to process more of the battery metal locally to maximize economic benefits and plans to ban the export of lithium concentrates from January 2027.

Sinomine operates two plants at Bikita with a combined capacity to produce 600 000 tonnes of spodumene concentrate and petalite concentrate. A recent technical upgrade is expected to boost Bikita’s yearly spodumene concentrate production capacity to 400 000 tonnes. Sinomine is also building a 100 000 tonne per year lithium sulphate plant at Bikita, anticipated to be completed in mid-2027.

cv.headline: Authorities suspend three Praia businesses over hygiene and safety violations
cv.dek: Three retail establishments in Praia were suspended following inspections that uncovered health risks, expired products, and illegal alcohol sales.
paragraphs: Three retail businesses in Praia have been suspended due to poor hygiene and other irregularities identified during an inspection operation by the Regional Command Santiago Sul and Maio. Authorities stated that conditions in some of the inspected spaces posed risks to consumer health. The operation also led to the seizure of expired products, alcoholic beverages without fiscal seals, and illegally produced aguardente known as “garrafinha.”

Further irregularities included the absence of price displays and operating hours, lack of business licenses, and missing health cards for employees. Inspectors also found improper food handling, inadequate labeling, pest infestations, poor ventilation, overcrowding, and accumulated waste. Additionally, some staff lacked proper training, and prohibited products were being sold.

The Inspectorate General of Economic Activities (IGAE) urged economic operators to comply with legal requirements for their activities. They warned that non-compliance could endanger consumer health and result in legal penalties, following the inspection of about two dozen retail establishments that concluded in the early evening.

cv.headline: MpD challenges prime minister's intelligence service delegation
cv.dek: The opposition MpD party declared the prime minister's decision to delegate powers over the Republic Information Service (SIR) to the Minister of Internal Administration.
paragraphs: Cape Verde's opposition party, MpD, has voiced strong opposition to Prime Minister Francisco Carvalho's delegation of powers concerning the Republic Information Service (SIR) to Carlos Miguel Sena Castro Teixeira, the Minister of Internal Administration. The MpD stated in a communiqué that this decision is "ostensibly illegal and unconstitutional," arguing it alters the established political-institutional model for the intelligence service.

According to the MpD, Law No. 70/VI/2005 and Decree-Law No. 55/2009 both stipulate that the SIR operates under the direct and exclusive authority of the prime minister. The party contends that this arrangement is crucial for democratic control over a service that operates in an area sensitive to citizens' rights and freedoms. The MpD also highlighted that the SIR lacks investigative powers, such as questioning or detaining suspects.

The opposition party views the transfer of SIR leadership to the Minister of Internal Administration as problematic, as this minister also oversees internal security and criminal police. The MpD believes this creates a "dangerous proximity" between the intelligence service and entities with powers to intervene in citizens' private lives, posing a risk to institutional balance and democratic legality. The party also disputes the legality of the delegation itself, citing a lack of sufficient legal authorization.

cv.headline: Cabo Verde Minister Secures Vice-Presidency of African Health Fund
cv.dek: Cabo Verde's Minister of Health, Lúcio Fernandes, was elected vice-president of the African Public Health Emergency Fund's Monitoring Committee during a recent meeting in Addis.
paragraphs: Cabo Verde has gained a new role in African public health, with its Minister of Health, Lúcio Fernandes, elected vice-president of the Monitoring Committee for the African Public Health Emergency Fund (APHEF). This election occurred during a meeting organized by the World Health Organization for the African Region (WHO Africa) in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.

In this new capacity, Cabo Verde will oversee the implementation and operation of the fund, working to strengthen its governance, transparency, and effectiveness in collaboration with other member states and the WHO. The presidency of the Committee will be held by John Mbadi, Secretary of the National Treasury and Economic Planning of the Republic of Kenya.

While the vice-presidency does not involve direct management of the fund or automatic financing for Cabo Verde, the Ministry of Health states it offers an opportunity to amplify the nation's voice in African decision-making forums. It also aims to promote the sharing of national best practices and deepen regional cooperation in preparing for, preventing, and responding to health emergencies.

cv.headline: Corda hosts first Apple and Quince Festival to boost local produce
cv.dek: The inaugural Apple and Quince Festival in Corda aims to celebrate local products, encourage farmers to increase production, ensure fairer prices, and reduce waste.
paragraphs: Corda is hosting its first Apple and Quince Festival, an initiative stemming from the community's work in agricultural production and agri-food transformation, according to Maria do Rosário, president of the Ponta d’Cinta Community Association. The festival seeks to value local products and producers, with the apple being a key symbol for the Corda community.

The event intends to motivate farmers to produce more by offering unified prices for their products, thereby strengthening the agricultural activity and reducing waste. Rosário noted that the association faces financial challenges in organizing the festival and that some producers are unable to exhibit due to a lack of products at this time of year, partly due to insufficient rain.

The festival program includes guided visits to apple trees for children and adults, donkey rides for children, and a round table discussion on innovation and entrepreneurship in fruit transformation. A product fair and tastings are also planned, despite the challenge of some exhibitors prioritizing the current tourist season over participation.

td.headline: Chadian medical order warns against informal circumcisions after three deaths
td.dek: The Moyen-Chari provincial council of the National Order of Physicians in Chad issued a warning today after three children died following a circumcision in Sarh's Kissimi.
paragraphs: Dr. Kambe Helngda Christophe, president of the provincial council, stated on August 27, 2026, from his office at Sarh's Modern Hospital, that the deaths occurred within twenty-four hours of the procedure. He emphasized that medical acts performed outside appropriate health settings carry risks and urged families to use only qualified professionals.

The Order stressed that circumcision is not merely a traditional act but requires strict hygiene, proper equipment, and infection prevention measures, including tetanus. Dr. Christophe warned that neglecting these precautions can lead to severe complications for children and advised parents against entrusting health procedures to unqualified individuals.

To prevent future tragedies, the Order recommends that parents seek services at Sarh's health facilities, such as the provincial hospital, district hospital, or health centers, where a surgeon is available for such interventions under proper medical conditions. The Order also called on untrained practitioners to cease their activities and requested administrative and judicial authorities to increase controls.

td.headline: Chad launches workshop on pastoral contingency plans for 13 provinces

paragraphs: The workshop, which began on Thursday, aims to enhance the ability to anticipate, prevent, and manage crises affecting pastoral communities and livestock systems. Around thirty participants from the concerned provinces are analyzing risks and vulnerabilities to create localized plans.

Mht Adoum Seid, representing the provincial delegate for Livestock and Animal Production, and Chérif Abakar Doutoum, head of mission for the supervising ministry, emphasized the importance of anticipation and active involvement from stakeholders in preventing pastoral crises.

Djingar Gaspard highlighted the strategic scope of this contingency plan, describing it as an essential tool to protect livestock and herders from future shocks. This initiative by PRAPS 2 seeks to strengthen the resilience of pastoral systems and populations in its intervention zones.

Coordinated by Dr. Mbadjivia Kabdana, the initiative offers medical consultations, screenings, and health education.

Medical teams, supported by staff from the Béré Adventist Hospital, are providing free medical consultations and screenings for blood sugar and high blood pressure. These services are accompanied by various health education activities for the community.

The meeting's theme addresses challenges in routine vaccination, epidemiological surveillance, and the quality of health data reporting. According to Dr. Djimadoum Dionadji, the chief medical officer for the district, these sessions provide a forum for discussion among those involved in implementing and monitoring health activities.

The chosen theme highlights the need to strengthen three key health system pillars: routine vaccination, epidemiological surveillance, and data reporting quality. Routine vaccination is a primary intervention to prevent avoidable diseases and reduce illness and death, especially among children under five years old.

td.headline: Chadian Ministry Seeks Firms for Soil Mapping Project
td.dek: Chad's Ministry of Agricultural Production and Industrialization is inviting specialized firms to conduct rapid soil characterization and create decision-making maps.
paragraphs: The Ministry of Agricultural Production and Industrialization, through the RENFORT project funded by IFAD, has issued a call for expressions of interest to select a specialized firm. This firm will be responsible for rapid soil characterization and developing decision-making maps within the intervention zones of the ILSA project.

The mission, estimated to last 60 days, aims to generate operational information to guide agroecological interventions, demonstration activities, and sustainable soil fertility management strategies. Interested firms must demonstrate expertise in cartography, soil analysis, geographic information systems (GIS), remote sensing, and/or digital agriculture.

Candidate pre-selection will be based on a 100-point grid, with 10 points for activity nature, 30 for general experience, and 60 for specific experience. Firms with at least three similar missions, particularly in pedological mapping or soil fertility assessment for recognized funders, will receive particular attention. Expressions of interest are due by September 18, 2026, at 12 hours, at the IFAD projects office in N'Djamena.

The Minister encouraged the center's teams to continue their efforts to strengthen existing systems and enhance Djibouti's position in regional animal trade, while adhering to sanitary standards. This focus aims to ensure the country's role in livestock exports meets international health requirements.

dj.headline: Djibouti urges parents to secure e-cigarettes from youth access
dj.dek: Parents are encouraged to keep electronic cigarettes out of reach of children and monitor behavioral changes to prevent underage vaping.
paragraphs: Djibouti authorities are calling for increased vigilance from parents and educators to combat the growing normalization of vaping among minors. The Agence Djiboutienne d'Information reports that young people are acquiring e-cigarettes directly, finding unattended devices, or receiving them from peers who obtained them from vendors disregarding age restrictions.

The issue extends beyond direct purchases, as some minors share e-cigarettes found or left by parents in school settings. This circulation among the youth highlights a collective responsibility for prevention, with parents asked to secure devices and observe their children for any changes in behavior.

Schools are also tasked with a crucial role, as teachers and administrators can reinforce awareness and educate students about the dangers of vaping. The message to young people emphasizes that e-cigarettes are not toys and should not become a habit, regardless of perceived harmlessness, peer influence, or flavor.

dj.dek: The port of Djibouti successfully docked the "Benjamin Franklin," a container ship with a capacity of 18,000 twenty-foot equivalent units (EVP), marking the largest vessel ever.
paragraphs: Djibouti's ports demonstrated their capability to handle very large ships by accommodating the "Benjamin Franklin," a container ship measuring 400 meters in length. This operation required the mobilization of four latest-generation tugboats, each with a traction power of 65 tonnes, and was overseen by a Djibouti port pilot.

The President of the Ports and Free Zones Authority of Djibouti (APZFD) stated on X that the port is capable of handling and maneuvering large vessels for clients, attributing this success to the skills, know-how, and expertise of their human capital. The tugboats Omar Dankali, Barkat Hamadou, Farah Hassan, and Saad Warsama were specifically deployed for this maneuver.

The successful docking of the "Benjamin Franklin," which is among the world's largest container ships, showcases the nautical and human resources available at Djibouti's ports. sz.headline: Green Mamba fans plan 3 500km Angola road trip
sz.dek: Green Mamba supporters are organizing an overland journey covering over 3 500km to attend their team's CAF Confederation Cup match in Angola on September 12, 2026.
paragraphs: Green Mamba's loyalists are preparing for a cross-continental road trip to support their team in the second leg of the CAF Confederation Cup preliminary tie against Clube Desportivo Primeiro de Agosto. The journey to Luanda, Angola, from Mbabane will cover over 3 500km and is expected to take more than two days of travel.

The Correctional Services outfit has invited interested supporters to register for the road trip at a cost of US$200, which is E3 200 in Eswatini currency. The Eswatini CAF envoys will first host the Angolan powerhouse at Somhlolo National Stadium on September four, 2026, before the reverse fixture in Angola.

The most direct overland route for fans will cross through three countries: exiting Eswatini via the Oshoek/Ngwenya border, traveling through Gauteng towards Botswana, then crossing into Namibia via the Mamuno/Trans-Kalahari border, and finally entering southern Angola through border posts like Oshikango/Santa Clara or Ruacana before reaching Luanda.

sz.headline: Eswatini darts duo advances to Region V gold final
sz.dek: Sandziso Nhleko and Mbali Sihlongonyane secured a spot in the final after a decisive 3-0 victory over Zambia in the Under-25s darts competition.
paragraphs: Eswatini's Under-25s darts team has reached the gold medal final at the African Union Sports Council (AUSC) Region V games in Gaborone. The duo of Sandziso Nhleko and Mbali Sihlongonyane achieved this milestone with a dominant 3-0 win against Zambia. Their teammates, Neliswa Mhlanga and Siphamandla Dladla, were eliminated in the semi-finals after a 3-0 loss to Zambia.

The competition, which began with an official opening ceremony on Tuesday, is being held at the Aquamarine Tide Hotel in Gaborone. Five nations, including Eswatini, initially kicked off the games, competing against players from Zimbabwe, Botswana, South Africa, and Namibia. Zambia joined the event today, August 27, after missing the initial team events.

Team Eswatini experienced mixed results on day one, Wednesday, August 26. The Senior Men's team bounced back from a 12-24 defeat to Botswana with a 23-13 win over Namibia. However, they later suffered a 30-6 defeat to South Africa, though this result showed an improvement from a 31-1 loss to South Africa in 2024.

sz.headline: Central Bank of Eswatini plans new E10 commemorative coin for 2028
sz.dek: The Central Bank of Eswatini announced a limited-edition E10 circulating commemorative coin to mark the country's 60th independence anniversary in September 2028.
paragraphs: Eswatini will introduce a new E10 circulating commemorative coin in 2028, as announced by Central Bank of Eswatini (CBE) Governor Dr. Phil Mnisi. The coin will celebrate the country's 60th Anniversary of Independence on September 6, 2028. The CBE launched a design concept competition for the coin yesterday at its Ezulwini complex, inviting artists, students, designers, cultural enthusiasts, and the public to submit concepts by October 26, 2026.

The initiative aims to provide a lasting symbol of independence and national pride, while also allowing the CBE to assess public acceptance of higher denomination coins. The E10 denomination was chosen because its banknote is widely used and experiences significant wear and tear, typically lasting one to five years. Coins, in contrast, remain in circulation for 20 to 50 years, according to Dr. Mnisi.

This shift to a more durable E10 coin is intended to improve the efficiency of the currency system by reducing the frequency of replacement due to physical deterioration. The minting of the commemorative coin is an approved operational project for the bank's 2026/27 financial year, supporting the CBE's mandate to issue and redeem currency and maintain its quality and reliability for the public.

sz.headline: Eswatini designers showcase commercial fashion potential at IP Runway event
sz.dek: The Eswatini Intellectual Property Office hosted a runway event to highlight the commercial viability of local fashion, furniture, and arts for international markets.
paragraphs: Eswatini's creative economy demonstrated its readiness for global markets at the recent IP Runway event, hosted by the Eswatini Intellectual Property Office (EIPO) under the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Trade. The event, titled 'IP Runway: The Business of Fashion, Furniture and Arts,' showcased local talent in the presence of Her Royal Highness Princess Sakhizwe.

Designers presented collections that blended traditional Eswatini motifs with modern styles, emphasizing the commercial potential of legally protected designs. Categories included Roots and Heritage, Contemporary and Streetwear, Formal and Evening Wear, NextGen, Upcycle and Innovation, and Fashion Complementaries, featuring brands like Kotini, Guzzani, Designs by Yanda, and Goodness Fashion.

The showcase served as a workshop for designers and underscored the need for structural investment, cross-border licensing, and international industrial scale within Eswatini's fashion ecosystem. Princess Sakhizwe noted that domestic support for Eswatini brands is crucial before expanding to global audiences.

sz.headline: Eswatini government rejects China's security claims, defends sovereignty
sz.dek: The Kingdom of Eswatini has stated it will not be coerced or destabilized by China's advisory for its citizens to leave due to security risks, asserting its sovereign right.
paragraphs: The Government of Eswatini has rejected claims by the People's Republic of China that the kingdom poses an exceptional security risk, following a Chinese travel advisory for its citizens. Acting Spokesperson Thabile Mdluli acknowledged China's right to issue consular guidance but regretted any suggestion that Eswatini is generally unsafe.

Mdluli clarified that a recent law enforcement operation, primarily involving Chinese nationals, targeted suspected organized cyber-related criminal activity. She stated this operation demonstrates the vigilance of Eswatini's law enforcement, not a failure of public security, and that the country remains peaceful and stable.

Eswatini maintains that its foreign policy and diplomatic relations are matters of sovereign national determination, seeking friendship with all nations. China's Foreign Ministry Spokesman Lin Jian cited rampant telecommunications fraud and online gambling in Eswatini as reasons for their travel advisory, stating risks to public order and safety are extremely high.

ga.headline: Gabon Central Purchasing Agency expands market access in Makokou
ga.dek: The Gabon Central Purchasing Agency (CEAG) launched a three-day Mega Market in Makokou, Ogooué-Ivindo, offering essential goods at accessible prices ahead of the August 30.
paragraphs: The Gabon Central Purchasing Agency (CEAG) held a Mega Market in Makokou from August 24 to August 26, providing residents with access to food and essential products at what it described as accessible prices. This initiative aimed to help counter high living costs in the region, coinciding with preparations for the National Liberation Day celebration on August 30.

The market's opening was attended by Senate President Huguette Nyana and Ogooué-Ivindo Governor Christiane Leckat. CEAG's Director General, Théophile Boutamba, stated that the agency's presence in Makokou demonstrates its commitment to bringing its offerings closer to populations outside of Greater Libreville.

This operation in Makokou follows similar deployments in Akanda, Nzeng-Ayong, Owendo, and PK areas in Estuaire, as well as in Port-Gentil and Minvoul. The CEAG aims for these Mega Markets to allow more people to access a diverse range of products at affordable prices, though the long-term challenge remains establishing regular supply mechanisms beyond temporary events.

ga.headline: Road accidents kill four people in Gabon in one day
ga.dek: Two separate road accidents on Tuesday, August twenty-fifth, 2026, resulted in four fatalities, prompting calls for increased vigilance on Gabonese roads.
paragraphs: Four people died in two distinct road accidents across Gabon on Tuesday, August twenty-fifth, 2026. The first incident occurred in the afternoon on the Pegnoundou-Tchibanga road in Nyanga province, where Papy Donald Boussougou, a thirty-seven-year-old Gabonese man, died in a motorcycle accident. Judicial sources reported that he was a manager at the Mougoutsi Departmental Council.

Initial findings suggest Boussougou lost control of his two-wheeler while traveling at high speed, leading to a violent fall. Authorities noted significant head trauma and nasal hemorrhage. His body was transported to a funeral home after the scene was processed.

The second accident, which also claimed two lives, took place in Essasssa on the same day. Investigations have been opened by competent authorities to determine the precise circumstances of both incidents, highlighting the need for greater caution, especially among two-wheel vehicle operators who are particularly vulnerable in crashes.

ga.headline: Gabonese journalist Rudy Hombenet dies two months after top award
ga.dek: Rudy Hombenet Anvingui, a journalist for L'Union newspaper, died in Libreville on August 27, 2026, just two months after being named Best Print Journalist at the Makongonio 2026.
paragraphs: Rudy Hombenet Anvingui, a prominent journalist with the daily newspaper L'Union, passed away in Libreville during the night of August 26 to August 27, 2026. Her death occurred two months after she received the award for Best Print Journalist at the Makongonio 2026, the Gabonese press awards, on June 28. She had worked for L'Union since 2015, following her studies at Omar-Bongo University.

Hombenet, who was born in Moanda, had over ten years of experience in journalism and was known for her focus on social issues, education, and health. In recent months, her columns in "Espace Santé" addressed concrete health topics relevant to daily Gabonese life, including tuberculosis, depression, malaria, self-medication, and hospital operations.

Her passing is particularly impactful as she was actively working and had recently gained significant public recognition. According to Gabonactu.com, she died at the Polyclinique El Rapha in Libreville two days after giving birth to a daughter, though the circumstances following the birth were not specified by a colleague.

gm.dek: The Chinese Embassy in The Gambia celebrated returning scholarship recipients and announced further educational cooperation, including new technical training facilities.
paragraphs: The Chinese Embassy in The Gambia hosted a Bantaba event for Gambian scholarship recipients and returning scholars, marking ten years since China and The Gambia resumed diplomatic relations. During this period, nearly 400 young Gambians have received Chinese scholarships in fields such as science, information technology, engineering, medicine, and public service. Twenty-five more Gambian students will travel to China in September for studies.

Chinese Ambassador Liu Jin praised Gambian graduates for contributing their skills to national development and encouraged new beneficiaries to return with knowledge beneficial to their country. Higher Education Minister Professor Pierre Gomez described the scholarships as an investment in people and The Gambia’s future, urging returning scholars to apply their skills to national development. Mamburey Touray, a new scholar, plans to study advanced software architecture to develop technology platforms for Gambian law enforcement agencies.

gm.headline: Dr. Ceesay affirms Gambian control over national security institutions
gm.dek: Dr. Ceesay, a government official, stated that The Gambia's national security institutions are Gambian-led and operate under national laws, dismissing claims of lost control.
paragraphs: Dr. Ceesay dismissed suggestions that Gambians have lost control of their security institutions, calling them “misleading and incorrect.” He stated that the Gambia Armed Forces, State Intelligence Services, Police Force, and Immigration Department are all headed by Gambians and operate within the national legal framework. He emphasized that ECOMIG's role is one of partnership, not control.

Dr. Ceesay explained that cooperation with ECOWAS partners strengthens The Gambia's capacity to address cross-border threats like terrorism, organized crime, human trafficking, and drug trafficking. He drew parallels with international examples such as NATO forces in Germany and American forces in Japan, where foreign forces coexist with strong national security institutions under sovereign governments.

The official urged Gambians to engage in a factual debate about ECOMIG's role, stressing that legitimate questions about regional cooperation should not be based on the false premise that cooperation equals control. He affirmed that ECOMIG is a security partner, not a substitute for Gambian institutions, and does not diminish Gambian sovereignty or determine national security policy.

gm.headline: Gambian society confronts rising tribalism and prejudice
gm.dek: A recent analysis highlights the increasing prevalence of tribal stereotypes and discrimination across public and private spaces in The Gambia, despite widespread intermarriage.
paragraphs: The Gambia faces a growing challenge with tribalism and other forms of prejudice, according to a recent report. Statements that are stereotypical, discriminatory, tribalist, sexist, or homophobic are commonly heard from various societal figures, including religious leaders, politicians, and public servants. These remarks often go unchallenged, leading to their normalization and reinforcement within communities.

The report indicates that since independence, The Gambia has not taken consistent steps to address harmful cultural aspects or foster a national culture of diversity and inclusion. Prejudice is particularly pronounced in politics, where competition for power and influence exploits religious, ethnic, gender, disability, and age differences to justify discrimination and exclusion.

Despite the celebration of intermarriage and strong joking relationships among ethnic groups, tribalism appears to be increasing. The analysis suggests that Gambians must consciously decide that all citizens are equal in rights and dignity, regardless of identity, and cleanse minds of bigotry to judge individuals by their character.

gn.headline: Court hears arguments in case against Central Bank union leaders
gn.dek: A court in Kaloum heard final arguments in the case against three union officials from the Central Bank of the Republic of Guinea, with a decision now pending.
paragraphs: The trial of Momo Camara, Aboubacar Sidiki Camara, and Aboubacar Yansané, leaders of the Central Bank of the Republic of Guinea (BCRG) union delegation, concluded its arguments on Thursday, August 27, 2026, at the Kaloum Court of First Instance. The three are accused of "contempt of agent, violence, and assault" following a complaint filed by Warrant Officer Daouda Sankhon.

During the hearing, the civil party's lawyer requested the court to find the defendants guilty and order them to pay 100 million Guinean francs in damages to his client. The public prosecutor also sought a guilty verdict for contempt, violence, and assault, recommending a fine of one million Guinean francs for each of the three defendants.

Defense lawyers argued that the accusations were not sufficiently established and asked the court to reject the public prosecutor's demands. The case has been adjourned for deliberation, and the court's decision is now awaited.

gn.headline: Makanéra Kaké supports anti-corruption efforts, urges due process
gn.dek: Former deputy Makanéra Kaké backs the government's anti-corruption campaign but stresses the importance of respecting legal procedures and the presumption of innocence.
paragraphs: Makanéra Kaké, a former deputy, voiced support for the government's anti-corruption drive on Thursday, August 27, 2026, during an interview with Télé 24. He emphasized the need for firmness against those who damage the economy through corruption, stating that corruption leads to deaths due to lack of resources.

However, Kaké cautioned against premature accusations, particularly regarding the recent dismissals of ministers Mory Condé and Mourana Soumah. He highlighted the principle of presumed innocence, arguing that it is better to free a thousand guilty individuals than to condemn one innocent person.

Kaké suggested that rigorous application of the organic law on finance laws could significantly strengthen prevention and control mechanisms against corruption. He believes that if this law is respected, it would become very difficult to embezzle funds, even if complete eradication of corruption is not possible.

gn.headline: Demoudoula bridge access road shows degradation signs
gn.dek: Four months after inauguration, the access road to the Demoudoula bridge connecting Ratoma and Lambanyi communes in Conakry is already showing signs of degradation.
paragraphs: The access road to the Demoudoula bridge, part of five metallic bridges inaugurated on April twenty-ninth, is experiencing early degradation. Torrential rains in the Guinean capital have caused the asphalt to crack near the railway sector, according to an on-site observation on Thursday, August twenty-seventh, 2026. Motorbike taxi driver Mamadou Aliou Sow expressed surprise at the rapid deterioration, stating the road significantly eases daily travel.

Local residents attribute the issues to both environmental factors and human activity. Halimatou Thiam, a resident, noted design flaws where poorly oriented gutters cause water to pool on the roadway during heavy downpours. Additionally, the management of runoff water is complicated by makeshift constructions near and within drainage channels, blocking the sanitation network and accelerating asphalt deterioration.

Further damage includes a height limit gantry, set at three point five meters, which was recently struck by an oversized heavy vehicle. A resident identified as DK emphasized the importance of civic responsibility, highlighting that accumulated waste and blockages in drainage channels contribute to the road's destruction. The Ministry of Public Works is urged to intervene to prevent further damage.

gn.headline: Opposition leader demands inquiry into Forécariah mass grave
gn.dek: Six unidentified bodies, found tied and blindfolded in a mass grave in Allasoyah, Forécariah, have prompted calls for an independent investigation from a Guinean opposition leader.
paragraphs: The discovery of a mass grave in Allasoyah, Forécariah, containing six unidentified bodies, has led to calls for an inquiry from opposition parliamentary group president Abdoulaye Kourouma. The bodies were found on August twenty-fourth, two thousand twenty-six, in Sabakhouré, tied and blindfolded, according to local sources present at their exhumation.

Kourouma stated on August twenty-seventh, two thousand twenty-six, that his group plans to question the Minister of Justice and the Attorney General to initiate investigations into the incident. He also emphasized the need for the Ministry of Security to play its role fully, according to an interview with Africaguinee.com.

However, Kourouma noted that immediate fieldwork by parliament is limited due to the current parliamentary calendar, with only the Assembly's bureau functioning. Another opposition deputy, Dr. Faya Milimono, also demanded an independent and credible investigation into the circumstances of the deaths, as reported by Mosaiqueguinee.

gw.headline: Guinea-Bissau voters consider constitution expanding presidential authority
gw.dek: Citizens in Guinea-Bissau will vote Sunday on a new constitution that would grant the president power to appoint and dismiss the prime minister and cabinet.
paragraphs: Guinea-Bissau is set to hold a referendum this Sunday on a new constitution that would significantly increase the powers of the presidency. The proposed changes would allow the president to appoint and dismiss the prime minister and cabinet, create or abolish ministries, and chair the Council of Ministers. Additionally, the president could dissolve parliament during a severe political crisis and dismiss the government under specific conditions.

The constitutional reform also aims to reduce the size of parliament from 102 seats to 65 and decrease the number of electoral constituencies from 29 to 12. Supporters argue these changes could restructure the nation's political institutions, while critics, such as Professor Manuel Nobre de Barros of Lusofona University, warn that the reforms could give the president virtually unchecked power by altering the balance between the executive and legislature.

This referendum occurs less than a year after military officers seized power, just before presidential election results were to be announced. The proposed constitution also introduces a new requirement for presidential candidates to have resided permanently in Guinea-Bissau for the five years prior to an election. General elections are scheduled for December, making this vote a key step in the country's transition from military rule to an elected government.

gw.headline: Tigres de São Domingos accuses FFGB of disrespecting club members' will
gw.dek: The Tigres de Fronteira de São Domingos management considers the Guinea-Bissau Football Federation's decision to recognize Mamadu Lenin Dabo as club president an "affront."
paragraphs: The management of Tigres de Fronteira de São Domingos stated on Wednesday, August 26, 2026, that the Guinea-Bissau Football Federation (FFGB) disrespected its members by continuing to recognize Mamadu Lenin Dabo as club president. This decision disregards the social bodies elected by the club's associates in January of this year, according to a note distributed to the press.

During the FFGB Ordinary Congress last Saturday near Bissau, Tigres vice-president Catenca Djeme was prevented from attending. The FFGB justified this by the presence of Mamadu Lenin Dabo, who continues to claim legitimacy to represent the club, a stance the Tigres management called unacceptable and damaging to the club's rights within national football structures.

The Tigres management declared it did not participate in the FFGB Ordinary Congress and does not consider itself bound by any acts from the meeting that affect its representation rights. The club also stated it reserves the right to use institutional and legal mechanisms to formally claim recognition of its legitimacy in all FFGB and Guinean Football Clubs League activities.
